Cloud data sits on AWS in Virginia or Frankfurt, chosen by the account’s regional domain, and an EU DPA is offered. The self-hosted edition (from $3,590, renewed yearly at half price) includes source code. CoPilot AI is on all plans, sends requests to OpenAI in the USA, and the terms let AI providers use content for development. Leaving the cloud means Excel exports or the API on a Vibe+ plan.
records.bandEvidence: Bitrix24’s about page (read November 2026) claims more than 15 million organisations, 600+ staff in 12 countries and 960+ partners in 90+ countries; the organisation count includes free sign-ups.
records.integrationNotes: Bitrix24 Market lists 760+ apps (700+ in a September 2026 vendor blog) plus built-in Google Docs, Office 365 and telephony connectors; the REST API with inbound and outbound webhooks is only on Vibe+ plans, and Essentials plans cap Market apps.
records.calendarSync: Two-way real-time sync of Bitrix24 calendar events with Google Calendar, Apple iCloud and Microsoft Office 365 on every plan, plus CalDAV connections and macOS Calendar via CalDAV; tasks with deadlines appear in the Bitrix24 calendar but sync is documented for events.
records.dataOut: Task lists export to Excel with selected or all fields, and import from CSV; daily backups kept 7 days (30 on Enterprise) with restore on Standard and above; REST API and webhooks only on Vibe+ plans after 30 November 2026.
records.caveat: The plan line-up changed on 1 September 2026: from 30 November 2026 Essentials plans lose the REST API and MCP server and get capped AI and Market apps unless the customer pays for Vibe+ (annual plans bought before 1 September keep their terms until they end). The security page still cites Safe Harbor and lists only AWS’s certifications.

value.review: Free with no user cap, then flat fees: $99 a month covers 50 users; Scrum and full time tracking need $199.

use.review: Tasks sit inside a crowded suite of CRM, chat, sites and HR tools, and new users face a dense menu.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, login history and branch accounts only on Enterprise from $399; certifications cited are AWS’s, not Bitrix24’s own.

flex.review: List, Kanban, planner, calendar, Gantt and Scrum views, automation rules, workflows, BI Builder and a 760-app marketplace.

control.review: A self-hosted edition, or AWS in Virginia or Frankfurt, but the AI terms let providers use content and ownership is unpublished.

portability.review: Task lists export to Excel and import from CSV, but the REST API now needs a Vibe+ plan.

commercial.vendor: Alaio Inc. of Alexandria, Virginia, USA contracts with most customers; Alaio Cloud Limited of Limassol, Cyprus with European ones; the terms are governed by Virginia law. Privately held. The Record reported in December 2023 that Bitrix24’s parent company, 1C-Bitrix, is headquartered in Russia; Bitrix24 did not respond to the report, and the vendor does not publish who owns the Alaio entities.
commercial.yearNote: 2012. Public release of the Bitrix24 cloud service in April 2012, per the vendor’s about page.
commercial.priceNote: Flat rate per organisation, not per user: Basic is $49 a month billed annually ($69 monthly) for up to 5 users; Standard $99 ($144) covers 50 users and Professional $199 ($289) covers 100. No per-user plan exists.
commercial.priceDagger: Flat rate per organisation, not per user: Basic is $49 a month billed annually ($69 monthly) for up to 5 users; Standard $99 ($144) covers 50 users and Professional $199 ($289) covers 100. No per-user plan exists. Shown as $9.90 a person: the cost for a ten-person team.
commercial.freePlanNote: Unlimited users (the help centre, updated October 2026, confirms; the pricing page markets it as for 1 to 2 users), 5 GB, one admin, task lists, Kanban and a limited Gantt view, but no task time tracking, project views or REST API; idle accounts are deleted after 50 days.
commercial.plans: Free; Basic $49, Standard $99, Professional $199 and Enterprise from $399 (250 users, tiers up to 10,000 users at $7,999) a month billed annually; each paid plan also has a Vibe+ version ($59, $120, $240, Enterprise from $480) adding REST API, unlimited Market apps and unlimited AI. Self-hosted: Business $3,590 (50 users) and Enterprise $24,990 (1,000+), renewed yearly at 50%.
commercial.hosting: AWS in the USA (Virginia) or the EU (Frankfurt, Germany); EU domains such as bitrix24.eu, .de, .fr, .it and .pl are hosted in Frankfurt, bitrix24.com in the USA. Enterprise adds two geographically distributed data centres. A self-hosted edition runs on PHP and MySQL on Linux, Unix or Windows servers.
commercial.security: The security page cites AWS’s ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, PCI DSS and HIPAA, not certifications held by Bitrix24 itself; TLS, two-step authentication and IP restrictions on all plans; SAML SSO and 180-day login history on Enterprise only; signed GDPR DPA for EU customers.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, and desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux.
commercial.ai: CoPilot (task descriptions, checklists, summaries, project agents) on every plan, limited on Essentials and unlimited on Vibe+ Standard and above. The AI terms name OpenAI as provider with requests processed in the USA, say AI tools may be switched on automatically, and allow AI providers to use content for development and improvement, while marketing pages say data is not used for training.

records.name: ClickUp
records.blurb: Task and project workspace with a deep Space, Folder, List hierarchy, 15-plus views, docs, chat, whiteboards and metered AI agents.
summary: ClickUp tries to replace a team’s task manager, documents, chat and whiteboard with one Workspace, organised as Spaces, Folders, Lists and tasks. It is sold to teams of every size, and its free plan is a common starting point for small companies.

Few rivals match its range: tasks carry custom statuses, fields and dependencies, and any List can be shown as a list, board, calendar, Gantt chart, table, timeline, workload or mind map. Sprints, native time tracking, goals and dashboards are built in. The cost of that range is density; settings overlap and new users often need a guided setup.

Between late October and November 2026 ClickUp replaced its Unlimited plan with Core at $9 a user and lifted Business to $17 a user on yearly billing, adding a $100 Max plan. Free stays usable for small teams but stops at 60 MB of storage and 100 automation actions. Business is where timeline, workload, dashboards and timesheets live. AI is now included as pooled monthly credits per user, with top-ups at $10 per 10,000 credits.

ClickUp holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and 42001 certificates, and offers residency in the US, Ireland, Australia or Singapore on Enterprise. It states that AI partners may neither train on nor retain customer data. Admins can export all tasks to CSV, and importers cover most rivals, though Docs cannot be bulk-exported.
records.bandEvidence: ClickUp announced in September 2025 that it had passed $300 million in annual recurring revenue and served over 20 million users (company press release, BusinessWire, 9 September 2025).
records.integrationNotes: The pricing page lists 50+ native integrations including Google Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Jira, Figma, Zapier and Make; Salesforce, Tableau and Azure DevOps are Enterprise only. Public REST API with webhooks on every plan, rate-limited to 100 calls a minute below Enterprise.
records.calendarSync: Google Calendar integration on every plan: two-way event sync with the Planner and Calendar views, plus task sync from a Space, Folder or List to a Google calendar. Outlook Calendar integration on every plan syncs events two ways with the Planner, but tasks are not sent to Outlook. A one-way iCal feed of tasks with due dates is available on every plan.
records.dataOut: Workspace owners and admins export task data from selected Spaces, Folders or Lists to CSV, including comments, time estimates and attachment hyperlinks (files themselves download per task as zip). On the new plans List view export is a trial on Core with no Table or Form view export; unlimited List view export starts on Business. Docs export one at a time to PDF, HTML or Markdown; bulk Docs export is not available. Public REST API (100 requests a minute per token below Enterprise) with webhooks; importers for Asana, Trello, Jira, monday.com, Todoist, Wrike and CSV.
records.caveat: ClickUp’s plans changed in October and November 2026: Unlimited became Core, Business rose to $17 a seat on yearly billing and AI add-ons were folded into credits. Existing Workspaces are being moved across gradually; ClickUp says their prices change no earlier than January 2027, at renewal, and some see no change.

value.review: A free plan with unlimited members and no seat minimum, but timeline, workload and dashboards now need Business at $17.

use.review: The five-level hierarchy, dozens of toggles and overlapping features take real setup before a team settles in.

enterprise.review: SAML, SCIM, audit trails, custom roles and data residency on Enterprise, with ISO 27001 and ISO 42001 certification.

flex.review: List, board, calendar, Gantt, timeline, table, workload, mind map, map and team views, plus automations and dashboards.

control.review: US, EU, Australian or Singapore hosting on Enterprise at no extra cost; no customer-managed keys or self-hosting.

portability.review: Admins export the Workspace to CSV with comments and attachment links; importers for Asana, Jira, Trello and monday.

commercial.vendor: Mango Technologies, Inc., trading as ClickUp. Privately held and venture-funded; headquartered in San Diego, United States.
commercial.yearNote: 2017. Public launch of the web app in 2017.
commercial.priceNote: Core, per user per month billed annually; $12 billed monthly. No seat minimum; the whole Workspace must be upgraded.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free Forever has unlimited members and tasks, Kanban, calendar and sprints, with time tracking and Gantt as trials, and caps storage at 60 MB, Spaces at 5 and automations at 100 actions a month.
commercial.plans: Free Forever $0; Core $9 yearly or $12 monthly; Business $17 yearly or $25 monthly; Enterprise by quote; Max $100 yearly or $120 monthly, per user per month.
commercial.hosting: AWS. Data residency for core Workspace data in the United States, Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Australia) or Asia Pacific (Singapore) on Enterprise at no extra cost. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
commercial.security: SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018, 27701 and 42001, PCI compliance, HIPAA support with a BAA on Enterprise. Google SSO on Business; Microsoft, Okta and SAML SSO, SCIM, session management and audit trails on Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, desktop apps for macOS and Windows, Chrome extension.
commercial.ai: ClickUp Brain, Super Agents, AI fields and the AI Notetaker run on pooled monthly credits: 500 per Workspace on Free, then 1,000, 1,500, 3,000 and 10,000 per user on Core, Business, Enterprise and Max. ClickUp states AI partners are prohibited from training on customer data and keep no copies (zero third-party retention).

records.name: TickTick
records.blurb: Personal task list and planner combining lists, Kanban, a timeline, calendar views, habit tracking and a Pomodoro focus timer.
summary: TickTick is a personal planner that puts a task list, a calendar, a habit tracker and a focus timer in one app. It is aimed at individuals who want to schedule their day as well as list what to do.

Tasks live in lists and folders with tags, sub-tasks, checklists and natural-language dates. The same tasks can be shown as a list, a Kanban board, a Premium timeline with durations, a calendar or an Eisenhower matrix, and a Pomodoro timer logs focus time against them. There are no custom fields, dependencies or automation rules, and sharing is limited to small groups on a list.

The free plan stops at 9 lists of 99 tasks, 2 members per shared list and a basic calendar. Premium costs $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month, up from $35.99 and $3.99 in mid-2026, and raises the limits to 299 lists of 999 tasks while adding the timeline, multiple calendar views, task duration and AI features. There is no team tier.

Data is held on AWS in the United States with encryption at rest and no region choice or certifications. The privacy policy says third-party AI providers process inputs but data is not used to train models. A CSV backup and an Open API make leaving possible, but attachments do not come with it.
records.bandEvidence: TickTick’s homepage claims use by “millions of people” without a figure; a ClickUp review updated 3 June 2026 (a competitor, so secondary) cites over 30 million users.
records.integrationNotes: Google Calendar, Outlook/Exchange and iCloud calendar subscriptions, Zapier, IFTTT, Siri and Google Assistant, plus one-click import from other task apps; an Open API with OAuth is documented at developer.ticktick.com, with no webhooks found.
records.calendarSync: Google Calendar “Subscribe” shows all of an account’s calendars in TickTick, and adds, edits and deletes sync back to Google; Google Calendar “Integration” syncs timed tasks in chosen lists to one Google calendar and turns events added there into tasks, both ways, up to 3 accounts. Outlook/Exchange, iCloud and CalDAV calendars can be subscribed, and a calendar URL publishes TickTick tasks one-way to other apps.
records.dataOut: Manual CSV backup from web settings on all plans, without attachments or images; the vendor also keeps AWS point-in-time backups. Open API (OAuth) for tasks and lists; import from other task apps via Settings.
records.caveat: Premium rose to $49.99 a year and $4.99 a month between July and October 2026 (archived pricing pages); most third-party guides and older App Store snapshots still quote $35.99 and $3.99.

value.review: A free plan with 9 lists, then Premium at $49.99 a year, about $4 a month, with no seat rules.

use.review: Quick add and smart lists make capture immediate, though habits, focus and matrix views add menus to learn.

enterprise.review: No team plan, admin console, SSO or audit log; sharing stops at 29 members per list on Premium.

flex.review: List, Kanban, timeline, calendar and Eisenhower matrix views with habits and focus timer, but no custom fields or automation rules.

control.review: Hosted on AWS in the United States only, no published certifications, and the privacy policy names no legal entity.

portability.review: A self-service CSV backup and an Open API exist, but the backup omits attachments and the API is thinly documented.

tt.note: A Pomodoro and stopwatch focus timer logs time against tasks with statistics by list, tag or task, but there are no timesheets, billable rates or time exports.

gantt.note: Timeline view on Premium only, which the vendor calls a lighter Gantt chart; tasks have durations but no dependencies.

commercial.vendor: Appest Inc., which TickTick’s Terms of Service name as the provider; the App Store lists Appest Limited as seller, and a Chinese edition is sold as Dida365. Privately held; no head office is published.
commercial.yearNote: 2013. First public release; TickTick’s own blog posts about the app date from 2013.
commercial.priceNote: Premium, $49.99 a year per person (under $4.17 a month); $4.99 billed monthly on the web checkout and the US App Store. The price rose from $35.99 a year and $3.99 a month between July and October 2026.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free covers 9 lists of 99 tasks each, 2 members per shared list, 5 habits, list and Kanban views, a basic calendar and the focus timer; timeline, multiple calendar views and AI need Premium.
commercial.plans: Free; Premium at $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month for one person. There is no team or business plan, only an education discount.
commercial.hosting: All databases and servers on AWS in the United States, per the vendor’s security page; no region choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: Data encrypted at rest and SSL in transit; no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or other certification published. The GDPR is mentioned only for third-party partners. No SSO, SCIM or audit log.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS and iPadOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, watch apps and a browser extension.
commercial.ai: AI features and an AI Assistant on Premium only. The privacy policy says third-party AI providers process inputs, conversation history can be deleted, and user data is not used to train models.

records.name: Todoist
records.blurb: Personal and small-team task list built on projects, labels and filters, with natural-language dates and list, board and calendar layouts.
summary: Todoist is a task list for one person or a small team, organised around projects, sections, labels and saved filters. It suits people who want to capture tasks fast and see what is due today, rather than plan multi-step projects.

Tasks carry due dates written in plain language, recurring rules, priorities, sub-tasks and deadlines. Projects can be shown as a list, a board, a calendar or a table, and Business adds shared team projects with roles. There are no custom fields, dependencies, Gantt chart or timer; anything beyond tasks and dates comes from its 130 or so integrations.

The free Beginner plan stops at five projects, three filters and a week of history, with no calendar layout. Pro at $5 a month billed annually lifts those limits to 300 projects and adds reminders, the calendar view and the AI features Task Assist and Email Assist. Business went up in December 2025 to $8 a seat billed annually.

Data is stored on AWS in the United States (Northern Virginia, per the Trust Center FAQ), with no region choice and no self-managed edition; the pricing page lists SOC 2 Type II on every plan, held since late 2025. AI runs through models on AWS Bedrock and Google Vertex AI, whose providers have committed not to train on the data. Leaving is workable: the API covers everything, but the in-app CSV export drops comments, labels and attachments, and backups with comments are paid-only.
records.bandEvidence: Todoist’s homepage claims 50+ million professionals, more than 1 million Pro users and 30+ million downloads, and its About page lists 108 staff (both checked November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: The integrations directory lists roughly 134 entries, including Google and Outlook Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Gmail, Outlook Mail, Zapier, Make, Toggl Track and Jira; a public REST API (v1) with webhooks, an MCP server and a CLI are documented.
records.calendarSync: Google Calendar and Outlook Calendar on all plans (Outlook was added in June 2025). Time-blocked tasks sync to a dedicated Todoist calendar; changing date, time, title or deleting those events updates the task. Other calendars show read-only inside Todoist. Pro and Business connect up to three calendar accounts.
records.dataOut: Per-project CSV export on all plans (no labels, comments, attachments or reminders); automatic daily backups on paid plans as ZIP of CSVs with up to 500 comments per task and attachment links, 21 kept, completed tasks excluded. Full REST API v1 with backup download and completed-task endpoints.
records.caveat: Business rose from $6 to $8 a seat (billed annually) for renewals from 10 December 2025; older third-party price lists still quote the earlier figure.

value.review: A usable free plan with five projects, then $5 a month for Pro and $8 a seat for Business, no seat minimum.

use.review: Quick add with natural-language dates means a new user is capturing and scheduling tasks within minutes.

enterprise.review: Business adds roles, central billing and team activity logs, but no documented SAML SSO, SCIM or audit export.

flex.review: List, board, calendar and table layouts with filters and labels, but no custom fields, timeline or built-in automation rules.

control.review: SOC 2 Type II since late 2025 and a GDPR DPA, but all data sits with AWS in the USA, one region.

portability.review: Free CSV export per project omits comments; paid backups add comments, and the full API is open on every plan.

commercial.vendor: Todoist Inc. (formerly Doist). Privately held and founder-led, remote-first since 2011 with 108 staff in 38 countries; incorporated in Delaware, USA.
commercial.yearNote: 2007. Founder Amir Salihefendić launched Todoist as a personal project in 2007; the company behind it formed later.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per person per month billed annually ($60 a year); $7 billed monthly. Business is $8 per user per month billed annually or $10 monthly since 10 December 2025.
commercial.freePlanNote: Beginner is free for one person with 5 personal projects, 5 people per project, 3 filters, 5 MB uploads and one week of activity history, but no calendar or table layout and no backups.
commercial.plans: Beginner is free; Pro is $5 per month billed annually or $7 monthly; Business is $8 per user per month billed annually or $10 monthly, raised from $6 and $8 on 10 December 2025.
commercial.hosting: AWS in the United States per the security page and privacy policy, which also lists Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud as US-based providers; the Trust Center FAQ names the Northern Virginia region. No EU region choice and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II, listed on the pricing page for every plan and stated in the help centre as of December 2025 (first announced in an October 2025 product update); GDPR compliance with a DPA via the Trust Center; TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit and AES-256 at rest. No SAML SSO or SCIM is documented by Todoist; Business has an admin console with roles and team activity logs.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, Apple Watch and Wear OS, plus browser extensions and email add-ons.
commercial.ai: Filter Assist and limited Ramble voice capture on the free plan; Task Assist, Email Assist and unlimited Ramble on Pro and Business. Models run via AWS Bedrock and Google Cloud Vertex AI, whose providers have committed not to use the data for training; the privacy policy says Todoist does not train generalised models on user data.

records.name: Wrike
records.blurb: Project and portfolio management for marketing, PMO and service teams: folders, projects and tasks with Gantt, workload, proofing and approvals.
summary: Wrike is a project management system aimed at organisations that run many concurrent projects, such as marketing departments, agencies and PMOs. Its buyers are usually operations leads standardising how dozens of teams plan, approve and report work.

Work sits in an unlimited folder and project hierarchy, with custom item types, workflows and statuses. Projects can be shown as boards, tables, Gantt charts and calendars, and the higher tiers add workload charts, resource bookings, job roles, budgets, file proofing and approval flows. Setup is the cost: Wrike itself recommends a guided deployment for teams of 20 or more.

The free plan, capped at 200 active tasks, suits a small group trying the board and table views. Team at $10 adds Gantt, calendars and dashboards but is capped at 15 users. Business at $25 brings time tracking, request forms and approvals, needs at least 5 users and annual billing, and seats are sold in groups of five. In January 2026 Wrike retired its Enterprise plan for new buyers in favour of Apex, and from April 2026 AI agents run on monthly action quotas.

Accounts are hosted in Santa Clara, California, or Paris, chosen by where the account is registered. Wrike holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and 27018, puts SAML SSO and audit reports on Pinnacle, and sells Wrike Lock for customer-managed keys. Its AI addendum says customer data is not used to train models. On Business and above a full account backup exports comments and attachments, but it cannot be restored into Wrike.
records.bandEvidence: Wrike’s about page (November 2026) cites more than 20,000 customer organisations, more than 2 million users and more than 1,000 employees; it is privately owned and publishes no revenue.
records.integrationNotes: The app directory lists about 60 integrations, including Salesforce, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, Adobe Creative Cloud, Power BI, Tableau, QuickBooks, Miro and Claude; Wrike Integrate and two-way Wrike Sync are paid add-ons. Open REST API with webhooks on all plans, plus an MCP server.
records.calendarSync: One-way iCalendar feeds from Wrike folders and projects into Google or Outlook; two-way Google Calendar sync only with the paid Wrike Sync add-on. No native Outlook integration.
records.dataOut: Excel export on all plans (no comments, descriptions or attachments). Account backup on Business, Pinnacle and Apex only: tasks, folders and projects with descriptions, comments and time logs, plus attachments through the full backup; once per 24 hours, and it cannot be imported back. BI export on Pinnacle and Apex. Open REST API with webhooks.
records.caveat: Wrike restructured its top tiers on 21 January 2026: Enterprise is no longer sold to new accounts, Apex replaces it, and many enterprise controls now sit on the quote-only Pinnacle and Apex plans.

value.review: Team at $10 caps out at 15 users; time tracking needs Business at $25 with a 5-seat minimum and annual billing.

use.review: Folder, project and workflow configuration is heavy; Wrike recommends a consultant for teams of 20 or more.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, user audit reports, custom access roles, IP allowlisting and budgeting on Pinnacle; BYOK through Wrike Lock.

flex.review: Board, table, Gantt, calendar, workload, dashboards, custom item types, approvals, proofing and request forms.

control.review: US or EU (Paris) hosting by region, and customer-held encryption keys through the paid Wrike Lock add-on.

portability.review: A Business-tier backup includes comments and attachments; the Excel export on every plan drops comments and descriptions.

sync.note: Included sync is a one-way iCalendar feed; two-way Google Calendar sync runs only through the paid Wrike Sync add-on, and there is no native Outlook sync.

commercial.vendor: Wrike, Inc. Privately held, owned by Symphony Technology Group since July 2023 (previously part of Citrix from 2021); headquartered in San Diego, United States.
commercial.yearNote: 2006. Founding year and start of the vendor’s own product timeline; Wrike does not give a separate launch date.
commercial.priceNote: Team, per user per month billed annually, for 2 to 15 users; Wrike publishes no monthly price. Business ($25, 5 to 200 users) is sold only on annual terms; seats come in groups of 5 up to 30, 10 up to 100 and 25 above.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free has unlimited users but only 200 active tasks per account, with board and table views and 2 GB of storage per account; no Gantt, calendar, dashboards or custom fields.
commercial.plans: Free $0; Team $10 (2 to 15 users); Business $25 (5 to 200 users); Pinnacle and Apex by quote. Prices per user per month billed annually, valid for purchases from 21 January 2026.
commercial.hosting: Wrike-operated data centres in Santa Clara, California (default) and Paris, France; since 5 May 2025 accounts registered from Europe are placed in Paris automatically, and a move goes through the account manager. The help centre also lists an Australian data centre (app-ap.wrike.com) without stating who is placed there. No on-premise edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001 and 27018, CSA STAR; GDPR and CCPA compliance. Google authentication on all plans; SAML 2.0 SSO, two-step verification enforcement, user audit reports, IP allowlisting and custom access roles on Pinnacle and Apex. Wrike Lock (BYOK) is a paid add-on.
commercial.platforms: Web, Windows, macOS, iOS, Android.
commercial.ai: AI Essentials (content editing, comment summaries, rule generation) on Team; Wrike Copilot and AI agents from Business with monthly AI Elite action quotas from 1 April 2026, larger on Pinnacle and Apex, with paid packs. Wrike’s AI addendum states it does not use customer data to train its AI or underlying models, nor allow others to.

records.name: Zoho Projects
records.blurb: Project management inside the Zoho suite: task lists, Kanban, Gantt with dependencies, timesheets, issue tracking and workflow blueprints.
summary: Zoho Projects is a project planner for teams that want Gantt scheduling, timesheets and issue tracking at a low per-seat price. It suits small and mid-sized organisations, especially those already using Zoho CRM, Books or Desk.

Work is organised into projects, phases, task lists and tasks, viewed as a classic list, Kanban board, Gantt chart or calendar, with a separate issue tracker for bugs. Blueprints model approval workflows, and Enterprise adds custom profiles, cross-project dependencies, critical path and baselines. Agile sprints live in a separate product, Zoho Sprints.

Pricing is among the lowest here: Premium is $4 a user per month billed annually and Enterprise $9, with no stated seat minimum. The free plan stops at five users and three projects, and time tracking starts on Premium. SSO, webhooks and portfolio dashboards wait for Enterprise.

Zoho runs its own data centres and assigns a region at sign-up, with migration between regions on request. Zia AI runs on Zoho’s in-house model, and Zoho says customer data is not used for training. The portal owner can export a CSV backup once a day, but the help centre does not say whether attachments are included.
records.bandEvidence: Zoho’s own timeline marks passing 100 million users across its products (zoho.com/aboutus, 2026); Zoho does not publish a separate user or customer count for Projects.
records.integrationNotes: The features page lists 45 integrations (21 Zoho apps such as CRM, Books, Sprints and Analytics, plus Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Zapier and Zendesk), with more in the Zoho Marketplace; there is a public REST API, webhooks from Enterprise, and a Zoho MCP server.
records.calendarSync: One-way subscription links (iCal and Google Calendar) push project tasks, milestones and events into Google, Outlook or Zoho Calendar; a Marketplace extension creates Google Calendar events from Zoho Projects. No two-way task sync.
records.dataOut: The portal owner receives a ZIP backup of the whole portal (started via Export CSV), once every 24 hours, kept for 15 days; module views export to XLSX or CSV; REST API; importers for Microsoft Project (MPP), XLS, CSV, JSON, Jira and Basecamp.
records.caveat: Export coverage is unclear: Zoho documents a CSV portal backup but does not state whether attachments, documents and comments are included.

value.review: A five-user free plan with Gantt, then $4 a user billed annually and no seat minimum; Ultimate tops out at $14.

use.review: Classic list, Kanban and Gantt are easy, but blueprints, custom modules and layout rules need an administrator’s setup.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, custom roles, portfolio dashboards and a sandbox from the $9 Enterprise tier, under SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.

flex.review: List, Kanban, Gantt and calendar views, custom fields and modules, blueprints, business rules and custom dashboards on Ultimate.

control.review: Region chosen at sign-up from Zoho’s own data centres (US, EU, India, Australia, Japan, Canada and others), with ISO 27001/27701.

portability.review: Owner-run CSV portal backup, XLSX/CSV module exports, a REST API and importers for MPP, CSV, JSON, Jira and Basecamp.

sync.note: One-way: an iCal or Google Calendar link pushes tasks, milestones and events into Google, Outlook or Zoho Calendar; changes there do not flow back.

commercial.vendor: Zoho Corporation. Privately held and never externally funded; founded in 1996 and headquartered in Chennai, India.
commercial.yearNote: 2006. Public launch of Zoho Projects; Zoho marked the product’s 18th birthday in 2024.
commercial.priceNote: Premium, per user per month billed annually; $5 billed monthly. No seat minimum is stated.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free covers up to 5 users and 3 projects with Gantt charts, subtasks and 5 GB of storage, but no time tracking or custom views.
commercial.plans: Free (up to 5 users, 3 projects); Premium $4 per user per month billed annually ($5 monthly); Enterprise $9 ($10 monthly); Ultimate $14 ($15 monthly, from 150 GB storage per organisation). The Zoho Projects Plus bundle is sold through sales; Zoho’s pricing data lists it at $15 billed annually ($16 monthly).
commercial.hosting: Zoho-owned data centres; the account’s region (US, EU, India, Australia, Japan, Canada, Saudi Arabia, UAE, UK, China) is set by the sign-up domain, with migration on request. No self-managed edition of Zoho Projects.
commercial.security: Zoho holds SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001, 27017, 27018 and 27701 across its cloud services. SAML SSO, two-factor enforcement and custom profiles and roles from Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps.
commercial.ai: Zia summaries, translation, task creation, insights and the Ask Zia chatbot by tier, running on Zoho’s own Zia LLM; Zoho states customer data is not used to train its models. An MCP server connects external AI models.

records.name: Coda (Superhuman Docs)
records.blurb: Coda, now sold as Superhuman Docs: doc-and-database pages with linked tables in table, card, calendar and timeline views, formulas and Packs.
summary: Superhuman Docs, called Coda until July 2026, is a document in which pages contain linked tables that behave like a database, so a doc can become a task tracker, roadmap or small app. It suits product and operations teams that want to build their own workflow rather than adopt a fixed one.

Any table can be viewed as a grid, Kanban cards, a calendar or a Gantt-style timeline, with formulas, buttons, automations and forms on top. Packs pull Jira, Salesforce or Slack data into tables and push changes back. There is no built-in time tracking, and dependencies that shift dates automatically arrive only on Business.

Billing counts only Doc Makers: Pro is $12 a month billed annually and Business $33, while editors are free. The free plan is generous for small docs but caps shared doc size, attachments and automations. Since the rename, paid plans bundle other Superhuman products, Grammarly on Pro and Mail on Business.

Data is hosted on AWS in the United States with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II; SAML, SCIM and audit logs are Enterprise-only. Third-party AI providers may not train on content, but only Enterprise customers’ AI inputs are excluded from improving Coda’s own AI. Leaving means CSV per table or the API.
records.bandEvidence: Coda’s about page (November 2026) claims 50,000+ teams and use at 80% of the Fortune 100; the wider Superhuman suite claims 40 million people, mostly through Grammarly.
records.integrationNotes: Packs connect Jira, Slack, Salesforce, Figma, GitHub, Google Calendar, Gmail and others with two-way sync tables; Coda cites 500 to 800+ integrations across its pages. Public REST API, Pack SDK and the Docs MCP server.
records.calendarSync: No native calendar sync. The Google Calendar Pack syncs events into a table and can create events from buttons; data refresh is manual on Free, daily on Pro and hourly on Business.
records.dataOut: Tables export to CSV; the public REST API and Pack SDK are open to all plans; Admin APIs for workspace-wide export and deletion are Enterprise-only. Version history runs 7 days on Free, 30 on Pro, unlimited on Business.
records.caveat: Coda was renamed Superhuman Docs on 8 July 2026; coda.io still works but coda.io/pricing redirects to Superhuman’s plans, and paid plans now bundle Grammarly, Go and (on Business) Mail.

value.review: Editors and viewers are free and only Doc Makers pay $12, so a team with a few builders pays little.

use.review: A blank doc with tables and formulas, so someone has to build the task tracker before the team can use it.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs and a SOC 2 Type II report, but all only on the quote-based Enterprise plan.

flex.review: Linked tables with any view, formulas, buttons, automations, cross-doc sync, Packs and AI views make almost any workflow buildable.

control.review: ISO 27001/27017/27018, SOC 2 Type II and HIPAA, but data is stored only in the United States; BYOK is listed as coming.

portability.review: Tables export to CSV and a full REST API is open on all plans, but bulk admin export needs Enterprise.

gantt.note: A timeline view plots table rows as Gantt-style bars; dependencies that shift dates automatically need Business, and there is no critical path.

sync.note: Only through the Google Calendar Pack, which pulls events into a table and lets buttons create events; tasks do not sync automatically.

commercial.vendor: Superhuman (Grammarly, Inc., renamed Superhuman in October 2025). Privately held, San Francisco, United States; Grammarly announced its acquisition of Coda in December 2024 and bought Superhuman Mail in July 2025.
commercial.yearNote: 2019. Coda left beta in February 2019 after a public beta announced in October 2017; the company was founded in 2014, per Superhuman’s own timeline.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per Doc Maker per month billed annually ($15 monthly); Editors and Viewers are free, so only people who create docs or pages are billed.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free keeps unlimited editors and collaborative docs with tables, forms and formulas, but limits shared docs to 50 objects and 1,000 rows, gives 1 GB of attachments per doc, 7-day version history and a low automation quota.
commercial.plans: Free; Pro $12 per Doc Maker per month billed annually ($15 monthly, Grammarly Pro included on annual); Business $33 ($40 monthly, adds Mail, unlimited automations and version history); Enterprise custom.
commercial.hosting: Amazon Web Services; Coda states it hosts services and stores data in the US, with cross-regional backups. No residency choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: ISO 27001, 27017 and 27018 certificates, SOC 2 Type II (report on Enterprise), SOC 3, HIPAA, GDPR and CCPA. AES-256 at rest with AWS KMS keys; BYOK listed as coming soon. SAML SSO, SCIM, audit logs (12 months via Audit API) and AI admin controls on Enterprise only.
commercial.platforms: Web; desktop and mobile apps (iOS and Android) on every plan.
commercial.ai: Docs AI assistant (beta, for Doc Makers), AI columns and blocks, AI views and pages, and a Docs MCP server for Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. Coda’s AI FAQ says third-party AI providers may not train on customer data, and that AI inputs and results are excluded from improving Coda’s own AI only for Enterprise customers.

records.name: GanttPRO
records.blurb: Online Gantt chart planner with auto-scheduling, critical path and baselines, plus board, list, calendar and workload views at higher tiers.
summary: GanttPRO is a web-based Gantt chart planner made in Poland, aimed at project managers who want critical path and baselines without Microsoft Project’s weight. Its pages now address construction, manufacturing and consulting teams as well as general project work.

Each project is a task hierarchy on a Gantt chart with dependencies, lags and leads, auto-scheduling, baselines and critical path on every plan. Board, list and dashboard views come with Core; calendar view, custom fields and saved filters start on Advanced; workload, portfolios, budgets and time tracking on Business. There is no rule-based automation, and AI is limited to generating a plan from a prompt, voice note or file.

Core costs $8 per user per month billed annually ($7 from 20 seats), Advanced $12 and Business $19, with monthly billing at $9, $15 and $24 and not offered for a single seat. Enterprise, with SAML SSO, custom roles and unlimited storage, is offered at $25 against a $35 list price, annual only and five seats minimum.

Data is hosted on Microsoft Azure in the EU, under ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and a GDPR DPA; OpenAI is the listed sub-processor for AI plan generation. Exports cover PDF, PNG, XML and Excel, and the API and webhooks give a route out, though comments and attachments have no documented bulk export.
records.bandEvidence: GanttPRO reports 800K+ users reached in 2022 and 1M+ projects completed, and the pricing page cites 1M+ project managers and 1,000+ reviews (ganttpro.com, November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: Slack, Microsoft Teams, Google Drive, OneDrive, Jira Cloud (Business and up), Google Calendar and Outlook feeds, and imports from MS Project, Excel and CSV; an API with webhooks on every plan.
records.calendarSync: One-way pushes to Google Calendar and Outlook calendars of a project’s tasks, your assigned tasks or milestones, filterable by status, priority and dates; updates can take up to 24 hours.
records.dataOut: Projects export to PDF, PNG, XML or Excel; portfolios, workload, task lists, reports and time logs have their own exports. Export is limited to account owners and admins. Imports from MS Project, Excel, CSV and Jira Cloud. API with key-based access and webhooks for task and time-log events.
records.caveat: Advertised per-seat prices depend on team size and the Enterprise price is a time-limited offer, so the figure a buyer sees will vary.

value.review: Core is $8 a seat with critical path and baselines, but calendar view needs $12 and time tracking $19.

use.review: A Gantt chart with drag-and-drop dependencies and auto-scheduling is usable within minutes; resource calendars take longer.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO and custom roles only on Enterprise, ISO 27001 certified, no SCIM or admin audit log documented.

flex.review: Gantt, board, list, calendar, dashboard, workload and portfolio views, with custom fields from Advanced and no automation.

control.review: ISO 27001:2022 and a GDPR DPA, with Azure hosting inside the EU, but no other region and no self-hosting.

portability.review: Projects export to PDF, PNG, XML or Excel and import from MS Project, but only admins can export.

sync.note: One-way: selected tasks or milestones are pushed to Google Calendar or Outlook, with changes taking up to 24 hours.

commercial.vendor: DPM Solutions Sp. z o.o. Privately held; registered in Kraków, Poland.
commercial.yearNote: 2015. First paid purchase ($9), as the vendor’s own story records; development began in 2014.
commercial.priceNote: Core, per user per month billed annually for teams of up to 15; $7 from 20 seats; $9 billed monthly, and a single seat is sold annually only.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; a 14-day trial of the premium features needs no credit card.
commercial.plans: Core $8, Advanced $12 and Business $19 per user per month billed annually ($7, $10 and $17 from 20 seats; $9, $15 and $24 billed monthly); Enterprise $25 as a limited offer against a $35 list price, annual only and 5 or more users.
commercial.hosting: Microsoft Azure servers in the EU region, with backups kept in the EU; AWS also appears on the sub-processor list for hosting and storage. No region choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: DPM Solutions holds ISO/IEC 27001:2022. TLS in transit, sensitive data encrypted at rest, geo-redundant file storage, daily backups, third-party penetration testing. Two-factor authentication on all plans; SAML SSO (Google, Okta, Azure AD, OneLogin) and custom roles on Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps.
commercial.ai: AI Gantt Chart Maker and AI Project Planner on all plans turn a prompt, voice note or file into a project plan. OpenAI Ireland is the listed sub-processor; the privacy policy does not address training on customer data.

records.name: Hive
records.blurb: Work management with many project layouts (Gantt, Kanban, table, calendar, timeline), built-in chat and email, and Buzz AI credits on every plan.
summary: Hive is a work management tool in which every project can be viewed as a Gantt chart, Kanban board, table, calendar or timeline, with chat, email and meeting notes in the same window. It targets mid-sized teams, especially marketing and agency teams that also want proofing and resourcing.

Projects hold action cards with subactions, custom fields and dependencies; portfolio and summary views roll several projects together. Buzz, the AI assistant, drafts content, summarises work and builds workflows. Much of the depth sits in optional apps: proofing, timesheets, resourcing, dashboards, a CRM and a finance module.

The free plan is usable for small teams, but Gantt, calendar and table views stop after 100 uses each. Starter at $5 caps a workspace at 10 members and 10 projects, so most teams need Teams at $12 billed annually. Each add-on then costs about $5 a user per month, so a team with timesheets, resourcing and SSO pays about $27 a seat.

Hive is SOC 2 certified; its privacy policy places data in the United States, and there is no residency choice. AI requests go to third-party models, and Hive says workspace data is not used to train them. Exports are per view in CSV or Excel; there is no single full-workspace archive.
records.bandEvidence: Hive’s about page (November 2026) claims more than 2 million people use Hive; its funding record ($1.4 million seed in 2016, $4 million in 2017, $10.6 million Series A in 2019) points to a modest company size.
records.integrationNotes: Native connectors include Slack, Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Jira, GitHub, GitLab, Salesforce, QuickBooks, Harvest, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box and OneDrive; the claimed 1,000+ integrations come through Zapier. Public REST API, an MCP server and a Claude connector.
records.calendarSync: Hive projects can be published as a calendar feed and viewed in Google Calendar; a connected Google or Outlook calendar shows its events inside Hive. Neither direction writes changes back.
records.dataOut: Per-view exports: Gantt to PDF, PNG, MS Project, Excel or CSV; calendar to images, Excel or CSV; table, status and team views to Excel or CSV, with every field except activity. Time and timesheet reports download separately. REST API; guided import from Asana, ClickUp, Jira, monday.com, Notion, Trello, Wrike and Smartsheet, plus CSV, JSON and MS Project.
records.caveat: The pricing page shows only yearly-billed prices in its static text; the $18 monthly Teams figure follows from the calculator’s stated saving ($576 a year for eight users), and the monthly Starter price is not shown.

value.review: A ten-member free plan and a $5 Starter tier, but timesheets, resourcing and SSO each add $5 a user to Teams.

use.review: Projects switch freely between familiar layouts, though the many apps, add-ons and AI toggles take an administrator to arrange.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO and Okta SCIM sit in a $5 security add-on, alongside SOC 2 and portfolio views, with no customer-facing audit log.

flex.review: Gantt, Kanban, table, calendar, timeline, matrix and portfolio layouts, custom fields, forms, workflows and dashboards.

control.review: SOC 2 certified with ISO 27001 hosting, but data sits in the United States with no residency choice.

portability.review: CSV or Excel export from every layout, MS Project from Gantt, an API and importers for eight tools; comments are not exported.

sync.note: One-way: a project can be published as a calendar feed to Google, and connected Google or Outlook events show inside Hive, but edits do not sync back.

commercial.vendor: Hive Technology, Inc. Venture-backed and privately held, based in New York City; raised a $10.6 million Series A led by Comcast Ventures in 2019.
commercial.yearNote: 2015. Earliest date on Hive’s own timeline: the company graduated from the AngelPad accelerator in 2015. No separate public launch date is given.
commercial.priceNote: Starter, per user per month billed annually, capped at 10 members and 10 projects; the Teams plan is $12 billed annually, and the page’s own calculator implies $18 billed monthly.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free allows up to 10 members, unlimited tasks and notes, 200 MB of storage and 1,000 AI credits a month, but Gantt, calendar and table layouts are limited to 100 uses each.
commercial.plans: Free ($0, up to 10 members); Starter $5 per user per month billed annually (up to 10 members, 10 projects); Teams $12 billed annually; Enterprise quote-only. Add-ons at $5 per user per month each: proofing, timesheets, resourcing, advanced dashboards, SSO and enterprise security, external users; Finance $12; Hive CRM $29 per seat.
commercial.hosting: Multiple geographically separated data centres with ISO 27001-accredited hosting; the privacy policy says data may be stored or processed in the United States and elsewhere. Hive does not name the provider, and offers no data residency choice or self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 certified (type not stated on the security page). SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin, ADFS, Google Workspace, Entra ID), Okta SCIM provisioning, granular permissions and full data erasure in the Enterprise Security add-on at $5 per user per month, included on Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; iOS and Android apps.
commercial.ai: Buzz AI on every plan with monthly credits (1,000 Free, 3,000 Starter, 5,000 Teams, custom on Enterprise) and paid top-up packs; requests are processed by third-party LLMs, and Hive says workspace data is not used to train third-party models.

records.name: Linear
records.blurb: Fast, keyboard-driven issue tracker for software teams, organised around teams, cycles, projects and initiatives, with coding agents built in.
summary: Linear tracks issues for product and engineering teams, grouped into teams, short cycles, projects and company-level initiatives. Its reputation rests on speed and restraint, and it is sold to software companies from start-ups to OpenAI-scale customers.

Issues appear in list and board layouts; projects sit on a timeline with milestones and dependencies, and cycles give each team a sprint rhythm. Triage, customer requests and Linear Asks (Slack and email intake) feed work in. What it leaves out is deliberate: no time tracking, no calendar view and no general custom fields. Since 2025 it has added agents, an MCP server and a cloud coding agent.

The free plan admits unlimited members but caps a workspace at 250 issues, so any real team pays. Basic at $10 a seat (yearly) removes the cap; Business at $16 adds private teams, guests, Insights and Asks. SAML, SCIM and the audit log need Enterprise.

Workspaces are hosted in the EU or the US, chosen at creation and fixed, although account and usage data always stay in the US. Linear holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 and offers a HIPAA BAA on Enterprise. Its June 2026 terms state it does not train models on customer data. Leaving means CSV exports without comments, or the API.
records.bandEvidence: Linear says more than 50,000 companies use it (linear.app, November 2026), up from 15,000 corporate clients reported at its $82 million Series C at a $1.25 billion valuation (Built In, June 2025).
records.integrationNotes: The integrations directory lists about 350 entries (November 2026), including GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Figma, Sentry, Zendesk, Intercom and coding agents such as Cursor and Codex; a public GraphQL API, webhooks and an MCP server on every plan.
records.calendarSync: One way only: each cycle’s schedule can be subscribed to from Google Calendar or downloaded as an .ics file. Issue due dates are not published, and the Google Calendar integration only reads out-of-office events into a user’s Linear status.
records.dataOut: Admins export all issues as CSV (fields only, no comments or attachment files); members export views up to 250 issues; projects, initiatives and members export as CSV separately; single issues copy as Markdown with comments. GraphQL API and webhooks on all plans; importers for Jira, GitHub Issues, Asana and Shortcut plus a CLI importer.
records.caveat: The free plan’s 250-issue cap makes it an evaluation tier rather than a permanent home, and monthly-billing prices are not shown on Linear’s own pricing page.

value.review: Free seats are unlimited but stop at 250 issues; Basic costs $10 and Insights and private teams need $16 Business.

use.review: Opinionated defaults, keyboard commands and fixed issue properties make it usable within an hour, with little to configure.

enterprise.review: SAML, SCIM, audit log, IP restrictions and HIPAA all sit on quote-only Enterprise; Business gets Google SSO only.

flex.review: List, board and project timeline, but no calendar, no general custom fields and dashboards only on Enterprise.

control.review: EU or US hosting chosen at workspace creation on any plan, with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001:2022.

portability.review: Issue CSVs omit comments and attachments, but the full GraphQL API is open on every plan and four importers exist.

gantt.note: The timeline shows projects with milestones and project dependencies, not individual issues.

sync.note: Cycle schedules subscribe as an iCal feed; issue due dates do not sync, and the Google Calendar integration only reads out-of-office events into Linear status.

commercial.vendor: Linear Orbit, Inc. Privately held, venture-backed (Accel, Sequoia); founded in 2019, a remote company with staff across North America and Europe, US-incorporated.
commercial.yearNote: 2020. Public launch on 30 June 2020, when sign-ups opened to all after an invite-only beta.
commercial.priceNote: Basic, per user per month billed annually; Linear’s page shows yearly prices only, and third-party trackers report $12 billed monthly.
commercial.freePlanNote: Unlimited members but only 250 issues, 2 teams and 10MB uploads; API, importers, agents and MCP access are included.
commercial.plans: Free $0; Basic $10 per user per month billed annually; Business $16 per user per month billed annually; Enterprise custom, annual billing only. Cloud coding agent sessions draw on separately bought AI credits.
commercial.hosting: Linear-operated cloud with a choice of EU or US region when the workspace is created, on every plan; the region cannot be changed later, and workspace info, user accounts, API keys and usage data are always stored in the US. No self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, GDPR, and HIPAA with a BAA on Enterprise only. Google SSO on all plans; SAML, SCIM, IP restrictions, domain claiming and the audit log on Enterprise. Data encrypted with TLS 1.2 in transit and AES-256 at rest.
commercial.platforms: Web, macOS and Windows desktop apps, iOS and Android.
commercial.ai: Product Intelligence (duplicate and team suggestions), Pulse summaries, the Linear Agent, agent platform and MCP on all plans; Triage and Code Intelligence on Business and Enterprise; the cloud coding agent and Loops consume pooled AI credits. Linear’s June 2026 terms say it will not train its own models on customer data, its providers are contractually barred from training, and zero-data-retention processing is required where supported.

records.name: MeisterTask
records.blurb: Kanban task boards with a list view, built-in time tracking and a Business-tier timeline, hosted in Germany.
summary: MeisterTask is a Kanban task manager from MeisterLabs, the Austrian-German company behind MindMeister. It is sold to small and medium teams, especially in Europe, who want a simple shared board with data kept in Germany.

Projects open as a board or a list; tasks carry checklists, tags, attachments, relationships and a built-in timer whose time slips export to CSV or Harvest. Section automations arrive with Pro. Subtasks, custom fields, roles and a Gantt-style timeline arrive with Business. There is no calendar view, and the Windows and Mac desktop apps were withdrawn in April 2025, leaving web, iOS and Android. Redesigned board, list and timeline views are rolling out in beta during Q4 2026.

The free Basic plan stops at three projects and two integrations. Pro costs €12.50 a seat billed annually, but most teams that outgrow a board will be looking at Business at €24. SAML SSO is held back for Enterprise, priced by quote.

Data sits in Frankfurt on Google Cloud under an ISO 27001 certificate, with a GDPR DPA from a German contracting entity. Meister AI uses Google and OpenAI models that, the vendor says, do not train on customer content; only Business admins can switch it off. Leaving means CSV exports per project plus the public API.
records.bandEvidence: Meister reports 40+ million users across its products (mostly MindMeister) and 60 staff on its about page, and the MeisterTask site claims 10,000+ companies (both read November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: About 20 direct integrations including MindMeister, Slack, Google Calendar, Gmail and Outlook add-ins, Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive and Zapier; GitHub and Office 365 Groups are being retired. A public REST API is open to all users, and an MCP server connects ChatGPT and Claude.
records.calendarSync: Pro and Business: Google Calendar integration syncs tasks out and accepts task-name and due-date changes back, but not new or deleted events. All plans: a one-way iCalendar feed of tasks assigned to you, used for Outlook and other apps.
records.dataOut: Per-project CSV export (tasks, assignees, due dates, checklists, comments) for all users; JSON export is a reusable template without comments, assignees or attachments; time tracking to CSV or Harvest; attachments only via per-task zip or a personal data export. Public REST API on all plans; importers for Trello, Asana and CSV or JSON templates.
records.caveat: Prices are published only in euros and vary by billing region; new board, list and timeline views are in beta and rolling out through Q4 2026.

value.review: Three free projects, then €12.50 a seat annually; subtasks, custom fields and the timeline wait for €24 Business.

use.review: A clean Kanban board with a per-task timer that a new team understands without training.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, portfolios and the workload planner are Enterprise only, and no SCIM provisioning is documented.

flex.review: Board, list and timeline views with automations and custom fields, but no calendar view or dashboards.

control.review: ISO 27001 certified with all data on Google Cloud in Frankfurt; EU-only, but no region choice or self-hosting.

portability.review: CSV exports include comments and checklists, Trello and Asana importers exist, but attachments need separate download.

commercial.vendor: MeisterLabs GmbH. Privately held, based in Vienna, Austria and Munich, Germany; founded in 2006, with Verdane leading a $52 million growth round in 2021.
commercial.yearNote: 2015. Public release of the web app in March 2015, announced by MeisterLabs.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per user per month billed annually; €15.50 billed monthly. Published in euros only, excluding VAT; about $14 at the November 2026 rate of $1.12 to the euro.
commercial.priceDagger: Pro, per user per month billed annually; €15.50 billed monthly. Published in euros only, excluding VAT; about $14 at the November 2026 rate of $1.12 to the euro.
commercial.freePlanNote: Basic allows 3 projects, 5 Content Manager seats, unlimited viewers, 2 integrations, 20MB files and 20 AI credits a month.
commercial.plans: Basic free; Pro €12.50 per user per month annually (€15.50 monthly); Business €24 annually (€31 monthly); Enterprise by quote. All prices exclude VAT and vary by billing region.
commercial.hosting: Google Cloud Frankfurt region, Germany; backups at multiple offsite locations in Germany. No region choice, no self-managed or on-premise edition.
commercial.security: ISO 27001 certified (MeisterLabs cites ISO 27001:2022); GDPR and CCPA compliant with a DPA. Business adds roles, IP-range restrictions and activity exports; SAML 2.0 SSO (Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace) is Enterprise only. No SCIM documented.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS and Android. Windows and macOS desktop apps were discontinued on 28 April 2025. Gmail and Outlook add-ins.
commercial.ai: Meister AI on all plans with monthly credits (20 Basic, 75 Pro, 350 Business and Enterprise): writing assistant, Ask Meister AI search and AI status updates. Uses a Meister search model plus Google and OpenAI models; the vendor says providers do not train on processed data. Only Business team admins can disable it.

records.name: Motion
records.blurb: A task, project and calendar tool that auto-schedules work into each person’s calendar, now sold to small businesses as an AI work suite.
summary: Motion began as an AI calendar that plans a person’s day by placing tasks into the gaps between meetings. Since 2025 it has been sold to small and mid-sized businesses as a work suite combining projects, docs, meeting notes and AI.

Tasks carry a duration, deadline and priority, and the scheduler rebuilds each calendar as things change. Around that sit projects with list, Kanban and Gantt views, custom fields, dashboards, workflow templates, docs and an AI notetaker. Its 2025 ‘AI Employees’ agents had their own pricing grid from August to November 2025; by November 2026 that page redirects to the homepage.

There is no free plan. Teams pay $19 a seat annually for Pro AI or $29 for Business AI, which adds Gantt, time tracking, capacity planning and permissions; a lone user pays more, from $29. Each seat carries a monthly AI credit allowance, with overage billed per 100 credits.

Data is stored on Google Cloud in Iowa, with no EU option. Motion holds SOC 2 Type II, sends AI requests to OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, and says it never trains models on customer data. There is no export button, so leaving means scripting the API.
records.bandEvidence: Over 10,000 B2B customers, mid-eight-figure ARR and 50+ staff (Motion, September 2025); the homepage claims ‘over 1 million’ users (November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: Native connectors are Google Calendar, Outlook 365, iCloud Calendar, Gmail, Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, Siri and Zapier (one-way, into Motion). A public REST API with an API key covers tasks, projects, comments, schedules and custom fields; no webhooks are documented.
records.calendarSync: Two-way event sync with Google Calendar, Outlook 365/Exchange Online and iCloud on all plans; Motion tasks appear on Google and Outlook calendars read-only. On-premise Exchange is not supported.
records.dataOut: No documented export of tasks or projects; calendar events can be imported from .ics. The public REST API (API key, rate limited) reads tasks, projects, comments, users, schedules and custom fields.
records.caveat: Motion sold an ‘AI Workplace’ and ‘AI Employees’ grid from August to November 2025, then returned to Pro AI and Business AI in December 2025 at the prices it had in spring 2025; those have held since. The founders’ Y Combinator listing now presents Wonderly, a separate software business for home-services firms that it says is funded by Motion’s cash flow; Motion itself is still on sale.

value.review: No free plan, $19 to $29 a seat annually, metered AI credits, and Gantt and time tracking held in the dearer tier.

use.review: Auto-scheduling only works once every task has a duration, deadline and priority, and the plan reshuffles itself as work changes.

enterprise.review: SOC 2 Type II and permissions on Business AI, but SAML SSO, SCIM and audit logs are not documented on any plan.

flex.review: List, Kanban, Gantt and calendar views, custom fields, dashboards, docs, workflow templates and a public API.

control.review: SOC 2 Type II and a GDPR DPA, but all customer data sits in one Google Cloud region in Iowa.

portability.review: No built-in task export; the API is the only way out, and no importers from other tools are documented.

tt.note: Time tracking is listed only on Business AI, the dearer of the two self-serve plans.

gantt.note: Timeline and Gantt charts are included only in Business AI; task dependencies feed the auto-scheduler.

commercial.vendor: NexusBird, Inc. (dba Motion), San Francisco, US. Privately held and venture backed: $75M raised in total, valued at $550M in September 2025.
commercial.yearNote: 2020. First public product under the Motion name, a browser focus tool covered in March 2020 after Y Combinator’s Winter 2020 batch; the AI calendar and task manager came later.
commercial.priceNote: Pro AI for teams, per seat per month billed annually; $29 billed monthly. A single-person Pro AI subscription costs more: $29 annually or $49 monthly.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; a free trial (individual or team) is offered before a paid plan starts.
commercial.plans: Teams: Pro AI $19 per seat billed annually ($29 monthly) with 7,500 AI credits per seat, Business AI $29 annually ($49 monthly) with 15,000 credits; individuals pay $29/$49 and $39/$69. Enterprise is by quote above 50 seats.
commercial.hosting: Google Cloud Platform, us-central1 region in Iowa, US; the vendor states data is not stored in the EU. No region choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II (audited by Prescient Assurance), report on request; encryption at rest and TLS in transit; GDPR DPA with SCCs. Permissions and access control on Business AI; SSO, SCIM and audit logs are not documented.
commercial.platforms: Web, macOS and Windows desktop apps, iOS and Android.
commercial.ai: AI chat, task and project planning, meeting notetaker and docs writer on both plans, metered by AI credits (7,500 or 15,000 per seat per month). Requests go to OpenAI, Anthropic and Google; Motion says it does not and never will train models on customer data.

records.name: Podio
records.blurb: No-code workspace where teams build their own apps of custom fields, then track them as tables, cards and calendars with workflow rules.
summary: Podio is a no-code work platform from Denmark, now owned by Progress Software after it bought ShareFile and Podio in October 2024. It suits small and mid-sized organisations that want to build their own trackers, such as CRMs, project registers or request queues, rather than adopt a fixed task model.

Workspaces hold apps that you design from fields: text, dates, categories, contacts, relationships and calculations. Items appear as tables, cards grouped by category, badges, activity streams or calendars, with comments, tasks and visual reports. Simple workflows arrive with Plus and if-this-then-that automation with Premium; there is no Gantt view and no built-in time tracking.

The free plan is only a trial in practice: five users and 100 items across the organisation. Plus at $11.20 per employee adds unlimited items, external clients and read-only users. Premium at $19.20 adds automation (25,000 actions a month), PDF generation and e-signature; extra API and automation capacity are paid add-ons.

Data is hosted on AWS in Dublin under SOC 2 Type II, with security policies Progress describes as conforming to ISO 27001. An AI Assistant is listed as coming soon on Premium, and an MCP server is in beta. Leaving is laborious: Excel exports omit comments and files, so a full copy needs the API or a backup extension.
records.bandEvidence: Progress markets Podio as ‘trusted by thousands of organisations’ and says Progress serves 200,000+ businesses (both November 2026); no Podio user or revenue figure is published.
records.integrationNotes: Built-in links to ShareFile, RightSignature, Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, OneDrive and Evernote, Zapier, plus an App Market and third-party extensions such as TimeCamp, Everhour, Globimail and Backup for Podio. Public REST API (1,000 calls an hour, more as a paid add-on), webhooks and a beta MCP server.
records.calendarSync: Personal, workspace or app calendars export one way to Google Calendar, Microsoft Exchange or an iCal feed; external calendars can be shown inside the personal Podio calendar, but edits in them are not synced back.
records.dataOut: Excel export per app or view, up to 20,000 items, excluding images, files, tasks, comments and activity; Excel import. Full backups via the REST API or the third-party Backup for Podio extension. API at 1,000 calls an hour, extendable with paid add-ons.
records.caveat: Podio is still sold, now by Progress Software after the October 2024 ShareFile purchase; its AI assistant is still marked ‘coming soon’ on the November 2026 pricing page.

value.review: Free stops at 100 items; Plus costs $11.20 per employee and real automation needs $19.20 Premium.

use.review: Every workflow begins by designing apps and fields, which suits builders more than people who just want tasks.

enterprise.review: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001-aligned policies, but SSO only through Google or Microsoft and no SCIM.

flex.review: Custom apps, relationship fields, visual reports and if-this-then-that workflows, though views stop at table, card and calendar.

control.review: SOC 2 Type II with data on AWS in Dublin; one region, no choice offered, and no ISO certificate stated.

portability.review: Excel export per app omits comments, files and tasks and stops at 20,000 items; full backup needs the API.

agile.note: Card layout groups items by a category field and lets you drag between stages; no WIP limits or sprints.

sync.note: Podio calendars push to Google, Exchange or iCal one way; external calendars can be overlaid on the personal calendar, but edits there do not flow back.

commercial.vendor: Progress Software Corporation. Publicly listed (NASDAQ: PRGS), based in the United States; Podio passed from Citrix (2012) to Cloud Software Group and then to Progress with ShareFile on 31 October 2024.
commercial.yearNote: 2011. Official launch in March 2011; founded in Denmark in 2009 as Hoist.
commercial.priceNote: Plus, per employee per month billed annually; $14 billed monthly. Once upgraded you pay for every employee, including the first five.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free covers up to 5 employees with unlimited workspaces and apps, but caps the whole organisation at 100 items and has no workflows.
commercial.plans: Free $0 (5 users, 100 items); Plus $11.20 per employee per month annually ($14 monthly); Premium $19.20 annually ($24 monthly). Paid add-ons raise API capacity from $23 a month and automation actions from $39 a month (annual).
commercial.hosting: Amazon Web Services in Dublin, Ireland, with backups in a separate AWS data centre. No region choice and no self-managed or on-premise edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II (report on request); Progress says Podio conforms to ISO 27001 security policies but does not state a certificate. HTTPS throughout, AES-256 encryption of files. SSO is limited to Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 identities, enforced per domain on paid organisations. User management, light users and read-only access on Plus; no SCIM; revision history and activity logs.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS (including iPad) and Android.
commercial.ai: An AI Assistant (beta) is listed as coming soon for Premium. A beta MCP server with 22 tools lets ChatGPT, Copilot Studio or Claude read and write Podio data. No published statement on training with customer data was found.

records.name: ProofHub
records.blurb: Flat-priced project tool for teams and clients: task boards, Gantt, table and calendar views, time tracking, chat, discussions and file proofing.
summary: ProofHub combines task management with team chat, discussions, notes and a review tool for marking up files and approving them. It is aimed at agencies, creative teams and companies that want one place for internal staff and clients.

Each project offers task lists as boards, a table, a Gantt chart with dependencies and baselines, and a calendar, plus timers and timesheets. Proofing and file versioning are its distinctive parts. There are no automation rules, AI features or dashboards beyond reports, and only seven integrations.

Pricing is flat for the whole account with unlimited users. Essential costs $45 a month billed annually but caps the account at 40 projects and 15 GB, and lacks custom roles, workflows, reports and the API. Ultimate Control is advertised at $89 a month billed annually, but that rate lasts three months before rising to $135. There is no free plan, only a 14-day trial.

The privacy policy says data is held in the United States, and ProofHub publishes no SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification and no SSO. Leaving means CSV exports task list by task list, calendar and timesheet downloads, or the API on Ultimate Control.
records.bandEvidence: ProofHub’s security page claims more than 90,000 companies and its customers page 85,000+ teams (November 2026); its about page lists 50+ employees and customers in 141+ countries.
records.integrationNotes: Seven listed integrations: Google Calendar and iCal, Slack, Box, Dropbox, OneDrive, QuickBooks and FreshBooks; a public REST API (v3) exists only on Ultimate Control, and no Zapier connector is listed.
records.calendarSync: One-way iCal subscription of a project calendar into Google, Apple or Outlook calendars; calendars can also be downloaded as iCal, CSV or PDF. No two-way sync.
records.dataOut: Tasks export to CSV one task list at a time; calendars as iCal, CSV or PDF; timesheets and Gantt charts export separately. No documented full account export. REST API v3 on Ultimate Control only; CSV task import and importers from Asana and Basecamp.
records.caveat: Ultimate Control’s advertised $89 a month is a three-month introductory rate; the standing price is $135 billed annually or $150 monthly.

value.review: Unlimited users from $45 a month suits big teams, but there is no free plan, and Ultimate Control rises to $135.

use.review: Boards, Gantt, chat and proofing sit in one conventional interface that new users and clients follow quickly.

enterprise.review: Custom roles, IP restrictions and activity logs on Ultimate Control, but no SSO, no SCIM and no certifications.

flex.review: Board, Gantt, table and calendar views, custom fields, forms and workflows, but no automation rules or dashboards beyond reports.

control.review: Data is held in the United States with no named certifications, and the privacy policy still cites the defunct Privacy Shield.

portability.review: CSV per task list, iCal or CSV calendars and timesheet exports, but no full account export; the API needs the top plan.

sync.note: One-way: a project calendar can be subscribed to as an iCal feed in Google, Apple or Outlook; nothing flows back.

commercial.vendor: ProofHub. Independent and founder-led (Sandeep Kashyap); lists its office in Covina, California, United States, and 50+ employees.
commercial.yearNote: 2012. Launch of ProofHub, per the vendor’s about page; it grew out of an earlier proofing tool, ProofMini, built in 2007.
commercial.priceNote: Flat rate for the whole account with unlimited users, not per user: Essential is $45 a month billed annually ($50 monthly) for 40 projects and 15 GB.
commercial.priceDagger: Flat rate for the whole account with unlimited users, not per user: Essential is $45 a month billed annually ($50 monthly) for 40 projects and 15 GB. Shown as $4.50 a person: the cost for a ten-person team.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; a 14-day free trial without a credit card, after which the account freezes until a plan is chosen.
commercial.plans: Essential $45 a month billed annually or $50 monthly (40 projects, 15 GB, unlimited users); Ultimate Control $89 a month billed annually or $99 monthly for the first three months, then $135 or $150 (unlimited projects, 100 GB, custom roles, workflows, reports, API).
commercial.hosting: Data collected, used and retained in the United States, per the privacy policy; no region choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: No published SOC 2, ISO 27001 or other certification; SSL in transit, encrypted database backups (live database unencrypted, per the privacy policy). No SSO or SCIM; IP restrictions, custom roles and detailed activity logs on Ultimate Control only.
commercial.platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps.
commercial.ai: None documented.

records.name: Remember The Milk
records.blurb: Long-running personal task list built on Smart Add, tags and saved-search Smart Lists, with reminders by email, text and push.
summary: Remember The Milk has been a web to-do list since 2005, run by a small independent team in San Francisco. It suits people who think in tags and saved searches and want reminders to reach them by email or text as well as push.

Everything is a list. Tasks get due dates, priorities, repeats, tags and nested subtasks, mostly typed in one line with Smart Add. Smart Lists are saved searches with almost 50 operators, and MilkScript lets Pro users script changes. There is no board, calendar view, timeline or timer.

The free Basic plan is usable for one person but limits sharing to two others, keeps only a week of completed tasks and leaves out subtasks. Pro costs $49.99 a year and adds Outlook task sync, Zapier, IFTTT, offline web use and the beta AI connector.

Data sits in data centres the vendor does not name, in several locations, and the privacy policy says it is transferred to the United States; there are no certifications. Leaving is straightforward: the account exports to JSON or iCalendar from settings, and a public API with webhooks is open for non-commercial use.
records.bandEvidence: The About page says more than 6 million people use its apps (undated, checked November 2026) and profiles two named staff plus a mascot; no revenue, customer or headcount figures are published.
records.integrationNotes: Gmail, Google Calendar (iCalendar), Outlook via MilkSync, Evernote, Siri, Alexa, Zapier, IFTTT, email, feeds, MilkScript and an MCP connector for AI assistants; a public API with webhooks for non-commercial use with an API key.
records.calendarSync: One-way iCalendar feed: Google Calendar and other apps subscribe to a private URL and see tasks on their due dates. MilkSync (Pro) syncs with Microsoft Outlook tasks, with a configurable sync direction. No calendar view inside the app.
records.dataOut: Account export from web or desktop settings to JSON (recommended as a full backup) or iCalendar (tasks and notes). Public REST API with webhooks, requiring an API key and limited to non-commercial use without an agreement.
records.caveat: The free plan keeps only 7 days of completed tasks and excludes subtasks, so most regular users end up on Pro.

value.review: A free plan with sharing for two people, then Pro at $49.99 a year, about $4 a month.

use.review: Smart Add is quick, but getting value from Smart Lists means learning nearly 50 search operators.

enterprise.review: A single-user tool: no team plan, admin console, SSO or audit log.

flex.review: One list view made flexible by tags, saved searches and MilkScript automation on Pro, but no board or calendar.

control.review: Data centres are unnamed and data is transferred to the United States, with no certifications; only encryption in transit is described.

portability.review: A self-service JSON export of the whole account plus iCalendar, and a documented API with webhooks, though commercial use needs permission.

sync.note: One-way iCalendar feed that Google Calendar and other apps subscribe to, showing tasks on their due dates; MilkSync for Outlook (Pro) syncs Outlook tasks, not calendar events.

commercial.vendor: Remember The Milk Inc. Privately held and independent, based in San Francisco, USA, with a distributed team; its founders came from Sydney, Australia.
commercial.yearNote: 2005. Public launch in October 2005, after work began in 2004, per the vendor’s About page.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, $49.99 a year per person (about $4.17 a month); no monthly option is listed.
