commercial.freePlanNote: The free Basic plan covers lists, tags, Smart Lists, reminders and sharing with up to 2 others, but drops subtasks, Outlook sync, Zapier, IFTTT, MilkScript and AI, and keeps completed tasks for 7 days.
commercial.plans: Basic is free; Pro is $49.99 a year. There is no team or business plan.
commercial.hosting: Remember The Milk servers in unnamed data centres in several geographic locations; the company is US-based and transfers EEA data under Standard Contractual Clauses. No region choice or self-managed edition.
commercial.security: HTTPS with Strict Transport Security for all traffic; no certifications, encryption-at-rest statement, SSO, SCIM or audit log published. Sign-in with Google, Apple or Facebook is offered.
commercial.platforms: Web, iPhone and iPad, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux (Ubuntu and Fedora) and Apple Watch (Pro).
commercial.ai: Beta “Connect with AI” on Pro links Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor through MCP to read and change tasks. The privacy policy says shared data is governed by the assistant provider’s policy and makes no statement about model training.

records.name: Taskade
records.blurb: Outliner-based workspace with eight project views, AI agents, automations and prompt-built apps; priced per workspace, not per seat.
summary: Taskade began as a collaborative outliner and task list and has since rebuilt itself around AI. It suits small teams and solo builders who want shared lists, docs and mind maps alongside AI agents and automations, at a flat workspace price.

Every project is a tree of tasks that can be shown as a list, Kanban board, table, mind map, Gantt chart, calendar, actionsheet or org chart. Tasks take due dates, assignees, custom fields and comments; the timer is a countdown rather than a time log. Since 2025 the product leads with Genesis, which builds small web apps, agents and automations from a prompt.

Free allows two users and no monthly AI credits. Paid plans are flat per workspace: Starter at $6 for three users (annual billing only), Pro at $10 for ten, Business at $25 for unlimited users with SAML SSO. AI credits (10,000 to 400,000 a month) are the real meter, and heavy AI use pushes teams up the tiers.

Data runs in a single AWS US East region. Taskade’s own security page says SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 and GDPR compliance are in progress and that it offers no signed DPA. Leaving means per-project Markdown or PDF exports or the REST API.
records.bandEvidence: Taskade’s homepage claims 1M+ users and 150,000+ community-built apps (November 2026); its about page lists 10 to 50 employees and a $5M seed round from October 2019.
records.integrationNotes: The help centre documents about 50 integrations, including Google Calendar, Gmail, Slack, Microsoft Teams, GitHub, Jira, Linear, Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce and Zapier, mostly as automation steps; the pricing page cites 100+. REST API, webhooks and MCP connectors are available.
records.calendarSync: Paid workspaces: two-way Google Calendar sync between Taskade and a managed ‘Taskade’ calendar (other Google calendars are not shown). All users: a one-way subscription feed for Apple, Google or Outlook.
records.dataOut: Per-project export as Markdown, plain text, PDF or image (mind maps, org charts, flowcharts); no documented workspace-wide JSON or CSV export. REST API (v1 and v2), webhooks and MCP. Importers for Trello, Asana, Notion, Todoist, ClickUp, monday.com, Evernote, Workflowy and others, plus CSV, Markdown, DOCX and PDF.
records.caveat: Taskade’s own security page says its SOC 2, ISO 27001 and GDPR work is unfinished and that it offers no signed DPA, which rules it out for many regulated or EU buyers.

value.review: Flat pricing: $10 a month covers 10 users on Pro, though the free plan has no AI credits.

use.review: The outline editor is immediate, but agents, automations and the app builder crowd the interface.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO on Business and SCIM on Enterprise, but SOC 2 and ISO 27001 are still in progress.

flex.review: Eight views over the same tree, custom fields, automations with branching, AI agents and generated apps.

control.review: One AWS US East region, no completed certification and, by its own statement, no signed DPA offered.

portability.review: Projects export one at a time as Markdown, text, PDF or image; bulk data out means using the API.

tt.note: A countdown and Pomodoro timer on tasks, with no logged time or time reports.

gantt.note: Gantt chart view sets task durations on a timeline, but no task dependencies are documented.

commercial.vendor: Taskade. Privately held, venture-backed US startup (Y Combinator S19, $5M seed in October 2019) founded in 2017 by John Xie, Dionis Loire and Stan Chang.
commercial.yearNote: 2017. Public beta launched on 5 December 2017, per Taskade’s about page.
commercial.priceNote: Starter, flat per workspace per month, sold on annual billing only ($72 a year) and covering up to 3 users. Pro is $10 a month annually ($20 monthly) for up to 10 users.
commercial.priceDagger: Starter, flat per workspace per month, sold on annual billing only ($72 a year) and covering up to 3 users. Pro is $10 a month annually ($20 monthly) for up to 10 users. Shown as $1 a person: the cost for a ten-person team.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free covers 2 users, one workspace, one AI agent, 10 automation runs a month and 250MB, with no monthly AI credits.
commercial.plans: Free $0 (2 users); Starter $6 a month, annual only (3 users); Pro $10 annually, $20 monthly (10 users); Business $25 annually, $50 monthly (unlimited users); Max $100 annually, $200 monthly; Enterprise $250 annually, $500 monthly, or custom terms through sales. Annual billing saves 50% on Pro and above.
commercial.hosting: Single AWS region (US East), described as a target rather than a contractual commitment; some AI providers operate outside the US, including in China. No region choice or self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 in progress, not completed; GDPR and CCPA alignment in progress; no signed DPA or SCCs offered. TLS in transit, AES-256 for backups and stored credentials. SAML 2.0 and OIDC SSO on Business and above; SCIM 2.0 on Enterprise; activity export on request, no tamper-evident audit log.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, Linux, and Chrome, Firefox and Edge extensions.
commercial.ai: AI agents, an AI assistant, automations and the Genesis app builder on every plan, metered by monthly credits (none on Free). Users choose among third-party models; Taskade says it contractually bars providers from training general models on customer data but cannot guarantee their compliance.

records.name: Teamwork.com
records.blurb: Project management for agencies and client-service teams: tasks, Gantt and boards plus time tracking, budgets, invoicing and resource planning.
summary: Teamwork.com manages client projects alongside the money behind them: time logged against tasks, budgets, retainers, invoices and staff capacity. It is sold to agencies, consultancies and other client-service firms that bill for their hours.

Each project offers list, board, Gantt and table views, with dependencies, milestones, subtasks, custom and formula fields, and a site-wide calendar. Clients can be invited into projects and approve files through Proofs. Resource planning, intake forms and invoicing from logged time arrive on Accelerate; quotes, multi-currency budgets and profitability reports need Optimize.

Pricing was restructured in 2026 into Basics at $9.99 and Accelerate at $24.99 per user per month billed annually, with three- and five-seat minimums. Most agencies wanting capacity planning land on Accelerate, at 2.5 times the entry price. AI features are bundled for an introductory period, with usage-based AI credits due to start in late 2026.

Every plan can host data in the US or the EU on AWS, and the company holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; SAML SSO costs extra below Enterprise. The vendor says customer data is never used to train third-party models. Leaving is workable: a full MySQL dump, CSV exports and a public API.
records.bandEvidence: Teamwork reported more than 20,000 customer businesses and 270 staff in its July 2021 funding release; Bregal Milestone’s portfolio page later lists about 300 staff; no newer figures are published.
records.integrationNotes: The vendor claims 150+ integrations, including Slack, Microsoft Teams, HubSpot, QuickBooks and Xero, with Salesforce and NetSuite only on Optimize; there is a public REST API (150 to 500 requests a minute by plan), webhooks and an MCP server.
records.calendarSync: Google Calendar and Outlook events appear in My calendar on Basics and above; editing those events and logging time from them needs Accelerate. Read-only iCal feeds can be added, and the site calendar can be exported. Tasks are not written to external calendars by the sync.
records.dataOut: A full raw MySQL backup of the site can be generated once a day; task, time and report views export to CSV/Excel; REST API with webhooks; importers from Asana, Basecamp, ClickUp, Monday, Trello and Wrike.
records.caveat: Plans were renamed and repriced in 2026 (Deliver and Grow became Basics and Accelerate), and the pricing page gives both September and November 2026 for the start of paid AI credits.

value.review: A five-user free plan, then $9.99 a seat with a three-seat minimum, jumping to $24.99 for automations and capacity planning.

use.review: Projects, budgets, rates and resourcing sit side by side, so getting value means configuring the client and financial setup first.

enterprise.review: SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001, SAML SSO with auto-provisioning on Enterprise or an add-on, but no documented SCIM.

flex.review: List, board, Gantt, table and calendar views with custom and formula fields, intake forms, automations and dashboards.

control.review: Every plan chooses US or EU hosting on AWS, backed by SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; no BYOK or self-hosting.

portability.review: A daily full MySQL backup, CSV exports and a complete API, plus one-click importers from six rival tools.

sync.note: Google and Outlook events flow into My calendar, but editing them back needs Accelerate and tasks are never pushed out to Google or Outlook.

commercial.vendor: Teamwork.com (Teamwork Ltd). Headquartered in Cork, Ireland; privately held, bootstrapped for 14 years before a $70 million investment from Bregal Milestone in July 2021.
commercial.yearNote: 2007. Founding year and first release of the project tool (then TeamworkPM) by Peter Coppinger and Dan Mackey in Cork.
commercial.priceNote: Basics, per user per month billed annually, minimum 3 users; monthly billing costs about 29% more by the vendor’s own figure, but the monthly rate is not printed in the page text.
commercial.priceDagger: Basics, per user per month billed annually, minimum 3 users; monthly billing costs about 29% more by the vendor’s own figure, but the monthly rate is not printed in the page text.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free covers up to 5 users and 5 projects with list, board, Gantt and table views, time logging and 100 automations, but only 100 MB of storage.
commercial.plans: Free ($0, up to 5 users and 5 projects); Basics $9.99 per user per month billed annually (minimum 3 users); Accelerate $24.99 (minimum 5 users); Optimize and Enterprise are quote-only.
commercial.hosting: Amazon Web Services in the US or the EU, selectable on every plan including Free; dedicated infrastructure on Enterprise; no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II and ISO/IEC 27001:2022; two-factor authentication and role-based permissions on all plans; SAML SSO with just-in-time provisioning on Enterprise or the paid Advanced Security add-on; no SCIM documented.
commercial.platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps; desktop apps listed on every plan.
commercial.ai: TeamworkAI (summaries, project wizard, AI assistants called Scout, Flo, Remi, Kash and Jack by tier) is included on paid plans for an introductory period before usage-based credits; an MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT and others. The vendor says data is never used to train third-party models.

records.name: YouTrack
records.blurb: Issue tracker and project tool with agile boards, Gantt charts, timesheets, a knowledge base and helpdesk; sold as Cloud or self-hosted Server.
summary: YouTrack is JetBrains’ issue tracker, which has grown into a project tool with a knowledge base and helpdesk attached. It is aimed at software teams first, though JetBrains also sells it to legal, marketing and support teams.

Issues carry custom fields and are driven by commands and a search query language. Agile boards run Scrum or Kanban, an interactive Gantt chart (redesigned in 2026.2) handles dependencies, and timesheets and time reports record logged work. Workflows are scripted in JavaScript. A calendar view is the main gap; it arrives through dashboard widgets or Marketplace apps.

The free tier covers 10 users and 3 helpdesk agents with nothing held back. Since 1 October 2025, Cloud costs $4.50 a seat annually or $5.40 monthly, still among the lowest in this category, and every subscription carries the same feature set.

Cloud instances live in one of four AWS regions (US West, Frankfurt, Ireland, Singapore). The self-hosted Server edition remains on sale, and administrators can download a Cloud database backup and restore it into Server. JetBrains states SOC 2 Type II. AI features route to OpenAI and Google, and JetBrains says AI usage data is not used to train models.
records.bandEvidence: JetBrains reports about 2,800 employees and 3 million customers across all its products (jetbrains.com company timeline, 2024); YouTrack’s own user count is not published, and its Marketplace lists about 97 apps (November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: Built-in integrations with GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket, Azure Repos, TeamCity, Slack and Zendesk, plus about 97 Marketplace apps and 19 dashboard widgets (November 2026); a full REST API, JavaScript workflows and an MCP connection for AI tools.
records.calendarSync: None native. Due dates can be shown in JetBrains’ Due Date Calendar dashboard widget; Google Calendar sync exists only as a third-party Marketplace app.
records.dataOut: Issue lists export to CSV or XLSX (500 issues by default, raisable by an administrator) including custom fields; articles export to Markdown or PDF. Administrators can download a full database backup and restore it into YouTrack Server. REST API on every plan; importers for Jira, Jira Service Management, GitHub, GitLab, monday.com, Zendesk, ClickUp, Confluence, Asana, Google Sheets, CSV and Excel.
records.caveat: Prices rose on 1 October 2025 for the first time since 2020, and JetBrains lists its SOC 2 scope only in its Trust Center, so YouTrack Cloud’s coverage needs checking there.

value.review: Ten free users with every feature, then $4.50 a seat annually, with AI, helpdesk and support included in the price.

use.review: Commands, a query language and custom workflows reward study; a newcomer meets dense settings before the board feels simple.

enterprise.review: SAML, LDAP and Active Directory login, audit events and granular permissions on every plan, but SCIM is not documented.

flex.review: Agile boards, interactive Gantt, timesheets, knowledge base, helpdesk, whiteboards, dashboards and JavaScript workflows in one licence.

control.review: Cloud in four AWS regions or self-hosted Server, with documented migration between the two in either direction.

portability.review: CSV and Excel issue export, a downloadable database backup that restores into Server, a full REST API and over a dozen importers.

calendar.note: No calendar view in the core product; JetBrains publishes a Due Date Calendar dashboard widget, and a full calendar comes from third-party Marketplace apps.

commercial.vendor: JetBrains s.r.o. Privately held and never venture-funded; founded in Prague, Czech Republic, in 2000, the maker of IntelliJ IDEA and Kotlin.
commercial.yearNote: 2009. First release of YouTrack in 2009, recorded as a new product that year in JetBrains’ company timeline.
commercial.priceNote: Cloud, per user per month on an annual plan ($54 a year) for teams above 10 users; $5.40 per user on a monthly plan, with volume discounts as teams grow. Prices from 1 October 2025.
commercial.freePlanNote: Cloud or Server free for up to 10 users and 3 helpdesk agents with unlimited reporters, with the full feature set, support and AI Assistant included.
commercial.plans: Free for up to 10 users; Cloud $4.50 per user per month annually or $5.40 monthly; helpdesk agents beyond 3 at $5.50 annually or $6 monthly; Server free for 10 users, then annual or perpetual user packs from 15 users (shown at EUR 900 a year for 15 users on JetBrains’ European store), with agents at $72 a year.
commercial.hosting: Cloud on AWS with the region chosen at creation: US West (Northern California), Europe (Frankfurt), Europe (Ireland) or Asia Pacific (Singapore); moves between regions go through support. YouTrack Server is a self-hosted edition, free for 10 users, with perpetual licences or annual subscriptions above that.
commercial.security: JetBrains states SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance, with report scope listed in its Trust Center; YouTrack Cloud’s inclusion in scope could not be confirmed on a public page. SAML 2.0, LDAP, Active Directory, Okta and other auth modules, two-factor authentication and an audit events log on every plan; SCIM is not documented.
commercial.platforms: Web, YouTrack Mobile for iOS and Android, and YouTrack Server for self-hosting.
commercial.ai: AI Assistant on all plans at no extra cost, using weekly free credits: issue and article summaries, alternative titles and comment rephrasing, sent through the JetBrains AI service to providers such as OpenAI and Google, and switchable per group. Built-in grammar and text features run internally. JetBrains says AI usage data is not used to train models that generate code or text.

records.name: Akiflow
records.blurb: A personal inbox and time-blocking planner that gathers tasks from email, chat and work tools and drags them onto your calendar.
summary: Akiflow is a planner for individuals who juggle tasks arriving from many places. It collects them into one inbox and asks you to time-block them onto your calendar, and it is sold mainly to founders, executives and other heavy schedulers.

Tasks arrive from Gmail, Slack, Notion, Jira, Asana, Linear and about a dozen other tools, then move to Today, Upcoming or a project, and onto the calendar as blocks. An AI assistant, Aki, answers in the app and on WhatsApp, plans days and reads meeting transcripts. There are no boards, Gantt or custom fields, and team features stop at shared availability.

There is one plan, Pro, at $34 a month monthly or $19 a month on an annual plan the vendor has labelled a promotion for a year. The trial lasts seven days and needs a card, and the AI Meeting Assistant costs $19 a month more. That makes it one of the dearest single-user tools here.

Data sits on Google Cloud in a region the vendor does not name, and Akiflow states it holds no SOC 2 or ISO 27001. There is no export button or public API, and in November 2025 support said backup and export were not on the roadmap. An OAuth MCP server is the only official programmatic route, so leaving is hard. AI features are opt-in, and an addendum says content does not train general-purpose models but may be used to debug and improve Akiflow’s own AI.
records.bandEvidence: No user or revenue figures are published; Y Combinator lists a team of 18 and the About page shows 12 people (both checked November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: 19 native connectors including Google, Outlook and iCloud calendars, Gmail, Outlook mail, Slack, Teams, Notion, Asana, ClickUp, Jira, Linear, GitHub, Trello, Todoist and Microsoft To Do, plus Zapier and IFTTT. No public REST API; an OAuth MCP server gives AI assistants read-write access.
records.calendarSync: Two-way event sync with Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar and iCloud Calendar on Pro: events can be created, edited and deleted in Akiflow; iCloud sync is periodic.
records.dataOut: No documented export or backup feature; support has pointed users to a SQLite export from a debug settings page. No public REST API; an OAuth 2.1 MCP server can read and write tasks, subtasks and events.
records.caveat: The $19 annual rate is labelled a promotion and could revert without notice, though the label has stood since at least November 2025. The AI addendum lets Akiflow use AI inputs to improve its own features, and the model provider is not disclosed.

value.review: No free plan, a card for the trial, and $34 a month monthly or a promotional $19 annually for one person.

use.review: Keyboard-first inbox and drag-to-calendar planning are quick to learn, but connecting and triaging many sources takes setup.

enterprise.review: No certifications, no SSO or admin console; team pricing is by quote but adds little beyond availability sharing.

flex.review: Lists, calendar, projects, tags and an AI assistant, but no board, custom fields or automation rules.

control.review: Google Cloud hosting in an unnamed region and no SOC 2 or ISO 27001, though certified under the EU-US Data Privacy Framework.

portability.review: No export feature or public API; support points to a SQLite dump from a debug page, and backups are off the roadmap.

tt.note: A focus timer exists, but its sessions are excluded from Stats, which report planned durations only.

commercial.vendor: Akiflow Inc., a Delaware corporation with a fully remote team ‘designed in Italy’; Y Combinator lists it in Spain. Privately held, backed by Y Combinator and Benson Oak Ventures.
commercial.yearNote: 2020. Year the company was founded and went through Y Combinator (Summer 2020); the vendor publishes no separate launch date.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per person per month billed annually ($228 a year); $34 billed monthly. The annual card has carried a PROMO label since at least November 2025, but no other annual price is published and the FAQ quotes $19 without qualification. Local purchasing-power pricing may apply at checkout.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan: a 7-day full-access trial that needs a card and converts to a paid subscription unless cancelled.
commercial.plans: One plan, Pro: $34 a month billed monthly or $228 a year ($19 a month) billed annually; the AI Meeting Assistant is a $19-a-month add-on, and team pricing is by quote.
commercial.hosting: Google Cloud Platform, region not stated; no region choice and no self-managed edition. The company participates in the EU-US, UK and Swiss-US Data Privacy Frameworks.
commercial.security: TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest. The vendor states it holds no SOC 2, ISO 27001 or FERPA certification. No SSO, SCIM or audit log.
commercial.platforms: Web, macOS, Windows, iOS, Android, Apple Watch and Wear OS. No Linux app.
commercial.ai: Aki, a chat and voice assistant in the app and on WhatsApp, plus auto-scheduling and AI project assignment, all included in Pro; the AI Meeting Assistant is a $19 monthly add-on. AI features are opt-in under a Privacy Policy Addendum for AI Features: content is not used to train or fine-tune general-purpose models beyond your organisation, but may be processed to debug and improve Akiflow’s AI and to personalise it. No model provider is named, and none appears in the sub-processor list.

records.name: Businessmap
records.blurb: Kanban-based portfolio and work management: boards, initiatives, OKRs, Gantt-style planning and flow analytics, sold as one plan with a 15-seat entry.
summary: Businessmap, called Kanbanize until 2023, grew from Kanban boards into a portfolio management platform that links OKRs and initiatives to the cards teams move each day. It is sold mainly to mid-sized and large organisations running Lean or Agile at scale.

Work lives on configurable Kanban boards inside workspaces, with initiatives above them on a Gantt-style planning view that supports predecessor links, critical path and milestones. A calendar shows deadlines, cards carry logged time with worklog reports, and flow metrics such as cycle time and blocked time are built in. Business rules automate moves and updates.

There is one feature-complete Standard plan and no free tier. It starts at 15 seats: $10.60 per user annually ($12.70 monthly), falling with volume. Automation rules and SSO cost extra, and Enterprise adds dedicated hosting and support.

Shared accounts are hosted on AWS in the US or the EU, with dedicated instances in other regions for large customers, and Businessmap states ISO 27001:2022 compliance. AI tools draft subtasks, comments and summaries through Azure OpenAI in Sweden or AWS, and the November 2026 privacy policy says this content is not used to train models. Data leaves through Excel exports and the REST API.
records.bandEvidence: Businessmap says it is trusted by 1,000+ enterprise PMO and portfolio teams and lists 300+ partners and offices in three countries (businessmap.io, November 2026); it publishes no user or revenue figures.
records.integrationNotes: Native integrations listed for Jira, GitLab, Bitbucket, Subversion, Power BI, Tableau, Looker Studio, Okta, Entra ID, OneLogin, Excel and Google Sheets add-ins, plus Zapier, Make and Power Automate; a REST API and a remote MCP server.
records.calendarSync: None native. The built-in calendar shows card deadlines and other dates inside Businessmap only; sync with external calendars needs Zapier, Make or Power Automate.
records.dataOut: Advanced search results export to Excel with configurable fields, links and subtasks; dashboard widgets export their data; Excel and Google Sheets add-ins import and export cards. REST API (with call limits on Standard) and a remote MCP server. Import is via spreadsheet templates; Enterprise includes free migration from other tools.
records.caveat: Prices come from the vendor’s live pricing calculator, which starts at 15 seats; there is no free plan, and automation rules and SSO add to the per-seat price.

value.review: No free plan, a 15-seat entry at $10.60 a seat, and automation rules and SSO both billed as add-ons.

use.review: Workflows, lanes, initiatives and WIP policies assume Kanban knowledge; most rollouts lean on training or the vendor’s consultants.

enterprise.review: SAML and OIDC SSO as an add-on, audit logs, granular roles, ISO 27001:2022 and dedicated infrastructure above 500 users.

flex.review: Boards, portfolio workspaces, Gantt planning view, calendar, OKRs, whiteboards, dashboards, flow analytics and IF-THEN business rules.

control.review: EU (Dublin, Frankfurt) or US hosting on shared plans, with dedicated AWS instances in other regions on request.

portability.review: Search results export to Excel and add-ins sync with Excel or Sheets, but there is no full-account JSON export.

commercial.vendor: Businessmap (formerly Kanbanize). Privately held and founder-led; offices in Sofia, Bulgaria, Bilbao, Spain and São Paulo, Brazil.
commercial.yearNote: 2011. Launched as Kanbanize on 1 January 2011; renamed Businessmap in October 2023.
commercial.priceNote: Standard, per user per month billed annually at the 15-user entry tier ($1,896 a year); $12.70 billed monthly; the rate falls to $8.50 annually at 100 users.
commercial.priceDagger: Standard, per user per month billed annually at the 15-user entry tier ($1,896 a year); $12.70 billed monthly; the rate falls to $8.50 annually at 100 users.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; a free trial with full features, including analytics, is offered instead.
commercial.plans: Standard (all features) from $10.60 per user per month annually or $12.70 monthly, sold from 15 seats; automation rules and SSO are paid add-ons; Enterprise is quote-only, adding a dedicated cloud instance, IP whitelisting, 1 TB storage and a customer success manager.
commercial.hosting: AWS: US (Virginia) by default for the Americas, Ireland or Frankfurt for EU customers; dedicated infrastructure (optional at 500 to 1,000 users, mandatory above 1,000) can be placed in Germany, Spain, São Paulo, Sydney and other regions on request. No self-managed edition.
commercial.security: ISO 27001:2022 and PCI-DSS compliance stated, twice-yearly third-party audits including penetration tests, TLS 1.2 in transit and AES-256 at rest. SAML and OIDC SSO with Okta, Entra ID or OneLogin as a paid add-on; audit logs and admin roles; IP whitelisting on Enterprise. No SOC 2 report was found.
commercial.platforms: Web, plus iOS and Android apps listed as “Businessmap formerly Kanbanize” (App Store and Google Play, both last updated in January 2026).
commercial.ai: AI Tools generate subtasks, comments, emails and summaries on cards; the AI Coach analyses workflow and card data; whiteboards add AI insights; included in the plan and switchable by an administrator. The privacy policy (updated 6 November 2026) says request content goes to Microsoft Azure OpenAI Service in Sweden or to AWS in the organisation’s data centre, and that neither Businessmap nor its AI providers use it to train models. A remote MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT and other clients query the account.

records.name: Celoxis
records.blurb: Project portfolio management for PMOs: scheduled Gantt plans, resource capacity, timesheets, costing and billing, in the cloud or on-premise.
summary: Celoxis is a project portfolio management system that has been sold since 2001, built in Pune for PMOs that run scheduled projects alongside resource capacity, budgets and billing. Its buyers are manufacturing, technology, healthcare and services firms rather than small teams.

Plans are task hierarchies with all four dependency types, constraints, baselines and critical path. Every report can be shown as a table, Gantt, calendar, card board with draggable lanes or chart, and dashboards are built from those reports. Timesheets with timers and approvals, expenses, risks and issues and custom workflow apps sit beside the projects. Scrum is handled by convention, with sprints as summary tasks, rather than as a dedicated mode.

Core costs $10 per full-access user per month billed annually, with a five-user minimum, and already includes workload tracking and capacity planning; timesheets cost $5 more on Core or come with Essentials at $25, which adds job roles and resource-conflict checks. Project billing, the client portal and an undefined “advanced security” bundle need Business at $45. Enterprise, which includes the on-premise licence, is quoted.

The cloud runs on AWS with a choice of US or Ireland data centres, under ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II, and a self-hosted edition runs on PostgreSQL, SQL Server or Oracle. The Lex assistant uses Microsoft Azure AI Services and is not priced separately. Exports are CSV and PDF; the REST API and webhooks are the fuller route out.
records.bandEvidence: Celoxis reports 500+ active customer organisations and more than one million projects run (celoxis.com, about page, November 2026), and 550+ G2 reviews.
records.integrationNotes: 21 integrations are configured inside Celoxis, including two-way Jira and Azure DevOps sync, Salesforce, QuickBooks Online, Slack, Okta and MS Project; Zapier and n8n cover the rest, beside a REST API, webhooks and a beta MCP server.
records.calendarSync: One-way: a calendar subscription URL publishes Celoxis events and task dates to Outlook (Open Calendar, From Internet) or Google Calendar, refreshed on the calendar client’s schedule.
records.dataOut: Gantt plans export to CSV; reports download as CSV (flat or grouped), PDF or image. Imports from MS Project (keeping dependencies and constraints) and CSV for tasks, users, clients and time. REST API reads and writes projects, tasks, time, expenses and custom fields, rate-limited from 150 requests an hour on Core to 1,800 on Enterprise; webhooks. On-premise customers hold the database.
records.caveat: The plan line-up (Core to Business) is new enough that third-party comparisons still quote older tiers; and the five-user minimum means the real entry price is $50 a month, billed annually.

value.review: Core is $10 with capacity planning, but a five-seat minimum applies and timesheets add $5 or need Essentials at $25.

use.review: A scheduling engine with constraints, work calendars and role-based privileges needs a trained administrator to set up.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO, roles and privileges, activity logs, portfolios and SOC 2 Type II, though no SCIM is documented.

flex.review: Gantt, card, calendar and chart outputs on any report, dashboards, formula fields and custom workflow apps.

control.review: A self-hosted edition on Linux, Windows or macOS, plus a choice of US or EU cloud on AWS.

portability.review: Gantt and reports export to CSV and MS Project plans import intact, but there is no full workspace export.

sync.note: A calendar subscription URL publishes Celoxis events and task dates to Outlook or Google Calendar; nothing comes back.

commercial.vendor: Celoxis. Privately held and founder-led (Nikhil Daddikar and Ravindra Wankar); head office in Pune, India.
commercial.yearNote: 2001. Launch of the web-based product after two years of development, as Celoxis’s own history records it.
commercial.priceNote: Core, per full-access user per month billed annually, minimum 5 users; timesheets are a $5 add-on on Core. No monthly-billing price is published.
commercial.priceDagger: Core, per full-access user per month billed annually, minimum 5 users; timesheets are a $5 add-on on Core. No monthly-billing price is published.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; a 14-day trial runs on the Business feature set, and paid plans add free client users plus 2 (Core) to 15 (Business) free read-only users.
commercial.plans: Core $10, Essentials $25, Professional $35 and Business $45 per full-access user per month billed annually, with cheaper team-member and timesheet-only seats from Essentials; Enterprise (including on-premise) is quoted.
commercial.hosting: Celoxis Cloud on AWS in the United States (default) or Ireland (EU), chosen at sign-up. A self-hosted edition runs on Linux, Windows or macOS with PostgreSQL 12+, SQL Server 2016+ or Oracle; on-premise releases follow the cloud by about a month, and moving from cloud to on-premise is charged.
commercial.security: ISO 27001 and AICPA SOC 2 Type II audited; EU and UK GDPR. SAML 2.0 SSO tested with Google, Salesforce, Okta, OneLogin, Azure and ADFS, with no plan stated; an undefined “Advanced security” item is listed only on Business and Enterprise. Two-factor authentication (in beta); role-based privileges; request logging and an activity log report. Encrypted snapshots every 30 minutes. No SCIM or customer-managed keys documented.
commercial.platforms: Web; iOS and Android apps for task updates, time logging and approvals.
commercial.ai: Lex, a natural-language assistant over live account data, not listed as a paid item on the pricing page; Microsoft Azure AI Services is the only listed AI provider. Neither the AI addendum nor the AI providers page says whether customer data trains models. A beta MCP server connects ChatGPT Desktop, Claude Desktop and Cursor.

records.name: Favro
records.blurb: Agile planning tool where the same cards live on Kanban boards, sheets, roadmaps and backlogs across teams; no free plan.
summary: Favro is a Swedish planning tool built by the founders of an earlier enterprise agile product. It is sold to teams that run several boards in parallel, especially game studios and software companies, and to managers who need to see across them.

Its distinctive idea is that one card can live on several boards at once, so a task appears on a team’s Kanban board, a manager’s sheet and a roadmap without copying. Collections group boards; backlogs nest cards into hierarchies; relations, dependencies, burndowns, dashboards, forms, documents and a calendar sit on top, and rule-based automations move work along.

There is no free plan. Lite at $5.10 a user is limited to five collections, 25 automation actions a month and no integrations or API, so most teams will need Standard at $6.80. Users are billed in buckets from two seats, and timesheets, SAML SSO and SCIM are Enterprise only.

Data stays in the EU on AWS Frankfurt and Cleura in Sweden, under ISO 27001 and 27701 certificates and a DPA. Favro has no built-in AI and charges no AI fees; an official MCP server lets Claude, ChatGPT or Cursor act on your behalf. Leaving means board-by-board exports or the API on Standard.
records.bandEvidence: Favro publishes no user, customer or revenue figures (checked November 2026); its site points to game-development, SaaS and enterprise teams, and its App Store listing carries 12 ratings.
records.integrationNotes: About 15 named integrations: Slack, Jira (with an on-premise proxy), GitHub, GitLab, Miro, Google Drive, OneDrive, Google and Outlook calendars, Zapier, Unito, Okta and OneLogin, plus an official MCP server since September 2026. API and webhooks on Standard and Enterprise only; Lite gets only primary integrations.
records.calendarSync: Each member can connect Google or Microsoft calendar so start and due dates of cards assigned to them appear there; one way, and only for cards assigned after connecting. A built-in calendar shows dated cards across collections.
records.dataOut: Board export to Excel, CSV or JSON from sheet view; whether comments and attachments are included is not documented. The REST API reads cards, comments, custom fields and dependencies. Importers for Trello, Basecamp Classic and CSV or Excel. API and webhooks on Standard (1,000 calls an hour) and Enterprise (10,000).
records.caveat: The year marks the first dated app release found; Favro does not publish a launch date, user numbers or revenue.

value.review: Cheap at $5.10 Lite, but no free plan, 2-user buckets, and Lite drops integrations, the API and reports.

use.review: Cards that live on several boards at once are flexible but take a team time to model well.

enterprise.review: Enterprise adds SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, collection management and timesheets; no audit log or portfolio layer is advertised.

flex.review: Boards, sheets, roadmaps, backlogs, calendar, dashboards, documents, forms, relations and 5,000 monthly automations on Standard.

control.review: ISO 27001 and 27701 certified with data held in the EU (Frankfurt and Sweden); no region choice yet.

portability.review: Boards export to Excel, CSV or JSON from sheet view, but the API is closed to Lite customers.

tt.note: Timesheet entries on cards and timesheet reports are Enterprise only; other plans have estimates and time-on-board only.

sync.note: Google and Microsoft calendar connections push your assigned cards’ start and due dates out one way.

commercial.vendor: Uppsala collaborative technologies AB, trading as Favro. Privately held, registered in Uppsala, Sweden; founded by Hans Dahlström, Erik Olofsson and Patric Palm, whose earlier agile-planning company was sold to a US acquirer.
commercial.yearNote: 2015. Earliest dated public release found: Favro AB’s iOS app on the App Store in July 2015.
commercial.priceNote: Lite, per user per month billed annually; $6 billed monthly. Sold in team-size buckets of 2, 5, 10, 25, 50 and 100 users, so a 3-person team pays for 5.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan; every paid plan has a 14-day trial without a card.
commercial.plans: Lite $5.10 per user per month annually ($6 monthly); Standard $6.80 annually ($8 monthly); Enterprise tailored pricing via sales. Minimum bucket is 2 users.
commercial.hosting: EU only: AWS in Frankfurt and Cleura (City Network) in Frankfurt and Sweden, with attachments in AWS S3. No region choice today; Favro says an Enterprise Plus plan will add it. No self-managed edition.
commercial.security: ISO/IEC 27001 and 27701 certified by a third party; PCI DSS SAQ A. TLS 1.2+ in transit, database and backups encrypted at rest. Google and GitHub OAuth on all plans; SAML SSO (Okta, OneLogin) and SCIM 1.0/2.0 on Enterprise. No audit log published.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, and desktop apps for macOS and Windows.
commercial.ai: No built-in AI features and no AI fees. An official MCP server (since September 2026) lets external assistants such as Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor act with the user’s own permissions; data handling then follows those assistants’ terms.

records.name: Fibery
records.blurb: No-code work platform where teams build their own linked databases, with docs, whiteboards, ten views, automations and AI on top.
summary: Fibery is a configurable workspace in which a team defines its own databases (tasks, features, clients, objectives) and links them, then works on them through views, documents and automations. It suits product teams, agencies and start-ups that want one tool shaped to their process.

Every database can be shown as a board, table, list, timeline with dependencies, Gantt, calendar, gallery, feed or map, with charts and dashboards over the data; whiteboards and collaborative documents link to entities. Rules, buttons and JavaScript scripts automate work. The cost of that freedom is set-up: nothing works until someone designs it, and time tracking is something you build.

The free plan covers 10 users and 10 databases. Standard at $12 a seat (annual) adds unlimited databases, charts and whiteboards; Pro at $20 adds custom apps, advanced permissions, JavaScript automations and shared Gantt views; Enterprise at $40, from 25 seats, brings SAML, SCIM and regional hosting.

Data is hosted on AWS in the EU unless an Enterprise customer chooses the US, UK or APAC, and Fibery holds a SOC 2 Type II report. Its AI terms forbid providers from training on inputs or outputs. Leaving is straightforward: a full Markdown and CSV export on every plan, plus REST and GraphQL APIs.
records.bandEvidence: Fibery reported 530 paid customers at the end of 2024 and 1.6 times as many in 2025, short of its 1,000-account goal, with a team of 30 (Fibery’s 2024 and 2025 year reviews; the latter published 21 January 2026).
records.integrationNotes: Built-in synced integrations with 20+ tools including Jira (two-way on Pro and Enterprise), GitHub, GitLab, Slack, Zendesk, Intercom, HubSpot and Google Calendar, plus Zapier and Make; public REST and GraphQL APIs, a custom-integration SDK and an MCP server.
records.calendarSync: One way into Fibery: the Google Calendar integration syncs meetings, holidays and other events into an Events database shown in calendar views, and Pro and Enterprise can sync several email and calendar accounts per user. Fibery entities are not pushed to external calendars and no iCal feed is documented.
records.dataOut: Export of the entire workspace as Markdown plus CSV on every plan; CSV import with field mapping; REST and GraphQL APIs, webhooks via automations, a custom-integration SDK and one-way Fibery-to-Fibery sync.
records.caveat: Fibery is a small company (30 staff and 1.6 times as many paid accounts in 2025 as the 530 it had at the end of 2024, short of a 1,000 target). It set itself the goal of profitability in Q3 2026 and has published no update since, which matters for a tool you build your processes inside.

value.review: Ten free users with real databases, then $12 a seat; SSO needs the $40 Enterprise plan with 25 seats minimum.

use.review: A blank workspace means designing databases, relations and views first; Fibery itself calls the people who do this Architects.

enterprise.review: SOC 2 Type II, audit logs and granular sharing, but SAML, SCIM and IP restrictions arrive only on Enterprise.

flex.review: Custom databases and relations, formulas, ten view types, charts, whiteboards, JavaScript automations and AI-built custom apps.

control.review: EU hosting by default with SOC 2 Type II; US, UK or APAC residency only on the Enterprise plan.

portability.review: Any plan can export the whole workspace as Markdown and CSV, with REST and GraphQL APIs and CSV import.

tt.note: Fibery offers time tracking as copyable templates: a lightweight tracker built from fields and action buttons, and a fuller Time Tracker Pro with time-log databases and formulas; there is no native timer or timesheet module.

sync.note: Google Calendar and other calendar accounts sync events into a Fibery database; nothing is written back to the external calendar.

commercial.vendor: Fibery Limited. Privately held, venture-funded ($8.3 million to date); founded in 2016 by Targetprocess co-founder Michael Dubakov, remote team with offices in Warsaw and Nicosia.
commercial.yearNote: 2019. Fibery 1.0 opened public registration in November 2019 after a private beta from early 2019.
commercial.priceNote: Standard, per user per month billed annually; $15 billed monthly. Observers and guests are free.
commercial.freePlanNote: Up to 10 users and 10 guests with 10 databases, unlimited entities, 1 GB of files, 250 automation runs a month and no AI credits; timeline, Gantt, whiteboard, feed, map, chart and dashboard views are private-only.
commercial.plans: Free for up to 10 users; Standard $12 per user per month annually ($15 monthly); Pro $20 ($24 monthly); Enterprise $40 ($50 monthly) with a minimum of 25 paid users. AI credits come with each paid seat (250, 500 or 1,000 a month by plan), and Pro and Enterprise can buy extra usage at $15 per 1,000 credits.
commercial.hosting: AWS (EC2 and RDS). EU data residency on all plans; Enterprise can choose EU, US, UK or APAC. No self-managed or on-premise edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 Type II report from an independent auditor (on request); GDPR DPA; data encrypted in transit (TLS) and at rest. Google login on all plans, Microsoft login on paid plans; audit log kept 14 days on Free, 90 days on Standard, unlimited on Pro and Enterprise; SAML SSO, SCIM, IP restrictions and session settings on Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web, macOS and Windows desktop apps, iOS and Android apps (released 2026), and Chrome and Firefox extensions.
commercial.ai: Fibery AI (answers, data changes, workspace configuration, semantic search, transcription and highlight finding) on Standard, Pro and Enterprise, metered by 250, 500 or 1,000 monthly credits per paid seat, with paid overage on Pro and Enterprise; the Free plan has no AI credits. A remote MCP server on every plan serves Claude, ChatGPT and other agents. Fibery’s AI Terms (October 2026) state it does not use customer data to train third-party foundation models and contractually bars AI providers from training on inputs or outputs.

records.name: Freedcamp
records.blurb: Project workspace of tasks, Kanban, calendar, time, files and discussions, with Gantt, wiki, CRM and invoices on paid tiers.
summary: Freedcamp is a long-running, low-cost project workspace from a small Californian company. It suits small businesses, schools and non-profits that want several teams in one place without per-seat bills, and offers discounts to education and non-profit users.

A project bundles separate apps: tasks shown as a list, Kanban board or table, a calendar, milestones, time tracking, discussions, files and a password store. Business adds a Gantt chart with dependencies, critical path and slack time, plus a wiki, issue tracker, CRM, invoices, reports, custom fields and custom statuses. There is no general rules engine for automation; recurring tasks are the main exception.

The free plan has no user or project cap, which is rare. Pro at $1.49 adds table view, subtasks, recurring tasks, Google Calendar push and cloud-file links, but most teams will want Business at $7.49 for the Gantt and custom fields. Guests and read-only collaborators cost nothing.

Data sits on AWS in the US; Freedcamp cites AWS certifications rather than its own and handles EU transfers through the Data Privacy Framework. Leaving relies on per-app XLS exports, which omit comments, or Business backups in XLS and XML with attachments, plus the public API.
records.bandEvidence: Freedcamp’s homepage claims ‘millions of users’ (November 2026) and the company once reported 2 million; Latka estimates revenue near $770K and 7 employees (July 2025, third-party estimate).
records.integrationNotes: First-party links to Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Slack, Google Calendar and email-in, plus Zapier for everything else. A public API is on every plan, and a hosted MCP server with 102 tools launched in 2026.
records.calendarSync: GSync on paid plans pushes Freedcamp calendars to Google Calendar one way; any plan can share a calendar link to Google, Outlook or Apple, which refreshes on the client’s schedule. External calendars are not brought in.
records.dataOut: Per-project XLS export of tasks, milestones, calendar, discussions, time and issues without comments or attachments; CSV Data Feed Links for tasks. Business (weekly) and Enterprise (daily) backups contain XLS, XML including comments, and attached files, kept for 30 days. Public API on all plans. Imports: tasks by XLS template only.
records.caveat: Company size and AI data handling are not published; the user count is a homepage claim and revenue figures come from a third-party estimator.

value.review: Unlimited free users and projects, then $1.49 Pro; Gantt and custom fields need $7.49 Business.

use.review: Each project switches on separate apps (tasks, time, wiki, CRM), which takes some setting up and learning.

enterprise.review: SAML SSO (beta) and white label on Enterprise, but no SCIM, audit log or certifications of its own.

flex.review: List, Kanban, Gantt, calendar and table views with custom fields and statuses; dashboards only on Enterprise.

control.review: Runs on AWS in the US with no own certifications; Enterprise can buy a private instance in a chosen region.

portability.review: Per-project XLS exports skip comments; XML backups with files need Business; imports accept XLS tasks only.

sync.note: GSync on paid plans pushes Freedcamp calendars into Google one way; other apps subscribe to a shared calendar link.

commercial.vendor: Freedcamp Inc. Privately held and founder-led (Angel Grablev); based in Santa Barbara, California, United States.
commercial.yearNote: 2010. Public launch of the web app in Santa Barbara, California, after development in 2009.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per user per month billed annually; $2.49 billed monthly. Read-only and guest collaborators are free on paid plans.
commercial.freePlanNote: Unlimited users, projects, tasks and storage (fair use) with 10MB files and the core apps; Gantt, custom fields, reports and backups need Business.
commercial.plans: Free $0; Pro $1.49 per user per month annually ($2.49 monthly); Business $7.49 ($8.99 monthly); Enterprise $16.99 ($19.99 monthly), with volume discounts through sales.
commercial.hosting: AWS, US-based hosting per the privacy and Slack data-retention pages; no region named. Enterprise can buy an isolated private instance hosted by Freedcamp in an AWS region of the customer’s choosing for a fixed extra yearly fee.
commercial.security: No SOC 2 or ISO certification of Freedcamp itself; the security page cites AWS’s ISO 27001, PCI and SOC reports, encryption in transit and at rest, and quarterly external audits. EU transfers under the Data Privacy Framework. 2FA from Pro; SAML SSO (beta) with Azure AD, Google, Okta on Enterprise; no SCIM or audit log published.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, Android, Windows and macOS desktop apps, plus a separate Freedcamp Chat app for iOS and Android.
commercial.ai: AI usage allowances by plan (Free minimal, Pro limited, Business high, Enterprise near-unlimited with a top model); an AI project-creation assistant generates tasks and due dates, and a hosted MCP server opens the workspace to external AI clients. No published statement on model training with customer data was found.

records.name: Nifty
records.blurb: Project workspace combining milestone roadmaps (Gantt), tasks, docs, files, chat and time tracking, sold per member or as flat team bundles.
summary: Nifty gathers a project’s milestones, tasks, documents, files and team chat in one workspace, with each project opening on a roadmap of milestones. It is aimed at agencies, product teams and small companies that work with clients.

Projects combine a Gantt-style milestone roadmap with task lists, Kanban and swimlane boards, and team calendars. Tasks carry custom fields, dependencies, story points and timers. Portfolios, workloads, goals and automatic check-ins roll work up across projects, and clients join as guests. Orbit AI drafts documents and generates projects and tasks.

Pricing comes in two forms: per-member plans (Pro $10, Business $16 billed annually) for small teams, and flat bundles (Pro $79 for 10 members, Business $124 for 30, Unlimited $399) for larger ones. The free plan admits unlimited members but only two active projects. Time tracking and custom fields start on Pro; the API and Microsoft SSO need Business.

Data sits on AWS under SOC 2 and ISO 27001:2022 audits, with no region choice. Orbit AI sends content to OpenAI, which Nifty says may not train on it. Leaving is harder than arriving: importers cover nine tools, but there is no documented workspace export.
records.bandEvidence: Nifty’s homepage and integrations page (November 2026) say 20,000+ teams have been onboarded; no revenue, headcount or funding figures are published.
records.integrationNotes: About 20 native connectors (Slack, GitHub, GitLab, Jira two-way, HubSpot, Google Drive and Calendar, Microsoft Suite, Zoom, Webex, Harvest, Toggl, Clockify, Typeform, Miro), Zapier for 2,000+ more, and an MCP server; the public API and webhooks need Business or above.
records.calendarSync: Two-way Google Calendar and Outlook sync: tasks assigned to a user appear in a chosen external calendar with name, description and date changes kept in step, and external events appear in Nifty’s calendar.
records.dataOut: No documented full workspace export; time tracking reports export to CSV or PDF and workload completion reports download. Public REST API and webhooks on Business and above; importers from Asana, Basecamp, ClickUp, Jira, monday.com, Todoist, Trello, Wrike and CSV/Excel.
records.caveat: Plans were re-cut in 2026 (plan IDs on the pricing page carry a 2026 suffix), and the choice between per-member and flat pricing changes the per-head cost sharply around seven people.

value.review: Per-member Pro at $10 suits small teams, flat bundles get cheap past seven people, but Free stops at two projects.

use.review: Each project opens on a familiar roadmap, task board and discussion, so small teams start quickly without configuration.

enterprise.review: SOC 2 and ISO 27001, Microsoft SSO from Business, but SAML only on Unlimited or Enterprise and no SCIM.

flex.review: List, Kanban, swimlane, Gantt roadmap and calendar views, custom fields, automations, forms, docs and dashboards.

control.review: SOC 2 and ISO 27001:2022 on AWS, but no named region or residency choice.

portability.review: Importers for nine tools, but no documented workspace export, and the API needs the Business plan or above.

commercial.vendor: Nifty Technologies, Inc. Privately held, based at 315 W 36th St, New York, United States.
commercial.yearNote: 2018. First public product launches on Product Hunt in September and October 2018; Product Hunt’s company profile dates the company to 2017.
commercial.priceNote: Pro per-member plan, per member per month billed annually ($16 billed monthly); teams of seven or more can instead pay a flat $79 a month billed annually for Pro with 10 members.
commercial.priceDagger: Pro per-member plan, per member per month billed annually ($16 billed monthly); teams of seven or more can instead pay a flat $79 a month billed annually for Pro with 10 members.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free allows unlimited members but only 2 active projects and 100 MB of storage, without time tracking, custom fields or automations.
commercial.plans: Free; per-member Pro $10 and Business $16 per member per month billed annually ($16 and $25 monthly); flat Pro $79 a month for 10 members, Business $124 for 30, Unlimited $399 for unlimited members (billed annually; $99, $149 and $499 monthly); Enterprise quote-only.
commercial.hosting: Amazon Web Services; Nifty names no region and offers no data residency choice or self-managed edition.
commercial.security: SOC 2 (Trust Services Principles, annual audits), ISO 27001:2022, CASA assessment, PCI Level 1 for payments, GDPR DPA. Google SSO and 2FA on all plans; Microsoft SSO from Business; custom SAML, IP restriction and white labelling on Unlimited and Enterprise. No SCIM documented.
commercial.platforms: Web; desktop apps for macOS and Windows; iOS and Android apps; Chrome extension.
commercial.ai: Orbit AI generates project templates, documents and tasks and builds workflows; it is powered by OpenAI, and Nifty’s privacy policy says submitted content may not be used to train OpenAI’s models. An MCP server connects external assistants.

records.name: Nozbe
records.blurb: Task manager for small teams built around projects, task comments and a personal priority list. List and calendar views only. EU-hosted.
summary: Nozbe is a Polish task manager built around task-based communication: discussion happens in comments on tasks rather than in chat or email. It is sold to freelancers and small teams, with industry pages aimed at lawyers, estate agents and agencies.

Work is organised as spaces, projects, sections and tasks, with an Incoming list for anything needing a person’s attention and a Priority list for their own day. A calendar view shows dated tasks, and AI can build a project from a description or a CSV file. There is no board, Gantt or custom field, and time tracking is manual fields only.

The free plan covers three people and three projects. Premium is $9 per user per month (annual) for a single space; Business at $15 adds one subscription across spaces and unlimited admins. Per-user prices fall from ten users.

Servers are at Hetzner in Germany, with backups and files on AWS in Paris and Frankfurt; a GDPR DPA is offered, but no certification or SSO. Nozbe AI uses Gemini; the vendor makes no statement on training. Task lists export to CSV, support will send a ZIP archive of all data, and a documented REST API makes leaving straightforward.
records.bandEvidence: Nozbe’s press page (read November 2026) says more than 700,000 people have used the Nozbe system; the about page lists 15 full-time staff and 10 contractors.
records.integrationNotes: Google Calendar, Outlook Calendar, Slack, Microsoft Teams, Dropbox, OneDrive, Evernote, email-to-task, Zapier and importers for Asana, monday.com, Todoist and Trello, on every plan; a REST API with an OpenAPI document, outgoing webhooks and an MCP server.
records.calendarSync: Two-way Google Calendar and Outlook sync on every plan: your dated tasks in active projects appear in a Nozbe sub-calendar, and events added to it become tasks. A one-way iCal feed per space is also offered.
records.dataOut: Project task lists and the calendar export to CSV (visible tasks only); printing to PDF; a ZIP archive of all projects, tasks and attachments on request to support; a REST API with an OpenAPI 3.0 document and outgoing webhooks. Data is quarantined for 30 days after cancellation, then deleted.
records.caveat: Nozbe raised the prices of both Nozbe and Nozbe Classic from February 2026, after letting customers lock in the old rate until the end of January. The original Nozbe, now Nozbe Classic, still runs for existing users but gets no new features; this record covers the current Nozbe, formerly Nozbe Teams.

value.review: A free plan for three people and three projects, then $9 a user, falling to $8 at ten users.

use.review: Projects, tasks, comments and a Priority list: a new team understands the model within minutes.

enterprise.review: Admin roles and member groups only; no SSO, SCIM, audit log or security certification is documented.

flex.review: List and calendar views with sections, tags and templates, but no board, Gantt or custom fields.

control.review: All data in the EU on Hetzner in Germany and AWS in Paris and Frankfurt, with a DPA but no certification.

portability.review: Task lists export to CSV, support sends a ZIP of everything, and the REST API and importers are on every plan.

tt.note: Manual ‘time needed’ and ‘time spent’ fields with section and project totals, on Premium and above; no timer or time reports.

commercial.vendor: NOZBE sp. z o.o., Gdynia, Poland. Privately held and owned by founder and CEO Michael Sliwinski; fully remote, with 15 full-time staff and about 10 regular contractors.
commercial.yearNote: 2007. Launch of the original Nozbe (later Nozbe Classic) in 2007; the current app, formerly Nozbe Teams, became the company’s main product in 2022.
commercial.priceNote: Premium, per user per month billed annually ($108 a year for one user); $11 billed monthly. Prices are set by team size and fall to $8 per user from 10 users.
commercial.freePlanNote: One space for up to 3 people with 3 active projects, 3 sections, 3 tags, 7 days of completed-task history and 500 MB of storage.
commercial.plans: Free (up to 3 users); Premium $9 per user per month billed annually ($11 monthly), one subscription per space; Business $15 ($19), one subscription across spaces with unlimited admins and storage. Both fall per user at larger team sizes, to $8 and $13 respectively.
commercial.hosting: Main servers at Hetzner in Germany; encrypted database backups on AWS S3 in Paris; uploaded files on AWS S3 in Frankfurt with backups in Ireland. EU only, with no region choice and no self-managed edition.
commercial.security: TLS in transit, encrypted files and backups, point-in-time restore on request, SMS two-factor sign-in on paid plans; no SSO, SCIM, audit log or certification is documented; GDPR DPA available to download.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS, iPadOS, Android, macOS and Windows.
commercial.ai: Nozbe AI creates projects from a description (powered by Gemini) and turns CSV files into projects (processed on Nozbe servers): 3 requests on Free, 1,000 on Premium, 2,000 on Business. A remote and local MCP server connects Claude, ChatGPT and Cursor. No statement on model training.

records.name: OmniFocus
records.blurb: A Getting Things Done task manager for Apple devices, with projects, tags, defer dates and perspectives; the web app is a paid companion.
summary: OmniFocus is the Omni Group’s task manager for people who run their lives by David Allen’s Getting Things Done. It is built for Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch and Vision Pro, and since 2019 the same database can also be reached from any browser.

Actions sit in projects and folders, carry tags, due, planned and defer dates, and can be sequential so only the next step shows. Custom perspectives filter the whole database, and a weekly review keeps it current. There are no boards, calendar grid, Gantt, time tracking or sharing. OmniFocus for the Web is a companion: you must set up the database in an Apple app first, and it lacks the review, notifications and repeat editing.

There is no free plan. The $99.99 annual subscription includes the Pro apps and web access. Owners of a $74.99 or $149.99 perpetual licence pay $49.99 a year more for the browser. For someone without an Apple device the web app is not usable on its own.

Sync uses end-to-end encryption with a passphrase you choose, and the Apple apps can sync through your own WebDAV server instead of Omni’s, though the web app cannot. There are no published certifications. The Apple apps export CSV, HTML and plain text; AI is limited to on-device Apple Intelligence date parsing and Siri in beta.
records.bandEvidence: No user or revenue figures are published; the About page lists 28 staff (November 2026), and OmniFocus has been a fixture of Apple-platform GTD since 2008.
records.integrationNotes: Apple-platform hooks: Siri (Siri AI beta in 2026), Shortcuts, Share Sheet, Apple Reminders capture, Mail Drop email capture and Omni Automation JavaScript plug-ins (Pro). No REST API, webhooks or Zapier connector; the web app has no integrations.
records.calendarSync: One-way: the Apple apps display device calendar events alongside tasks in Forecast. Tasks are not pushed to calendars, and calendar integration is not available in OmniFocus for the Web.
records.dataOut: The Apple apps export to CSV, HTML and plain text, keep automatic backups and allow database migration; Omni Automation (Pro) and AppleScript (Mac) script the data on device. No REST API. The web app can view and download attachments but has no export.
records.caveat: OmniFocus for the Web is not a standalone product: it needs a database first set up in an Apple app, and it lacks review, notifications and repeat editing.

value.review: No free plan; $99.99 a year covers every Apple device and the web, or $49.99 a year on top of a licence.

use.review: Defer dates, sequential projects and perspectives reward GTD practitioners but take weeks to learn; web setup needs an Apple device.

enterprise.review: A single-user tool: no shared projects, admin console, SSO or certifications; business purchasing is just volume licensing.

flex.review: Custom perspectives and Omni Automation scripting go deep, but every view is an outline, and the web lacks review and repeats.

control.review: End-to-end encryption with your own passphrase and optional self-hosted WebDAV sync, though the web app requires Omni’s sync server.

portability.review: CSV, HTML and plain-text exports plus automatic backups in the Apple apps; no REST API and no export from the web.

calendar.note: Forecast is a day-by-day list of due, planned and flagged items, not a calendar grid; on the web it shows tasks only.

sync.note: The Apple apps show device calendar events in Forecast, one-way and read-only; tasks are not written to calendars, and the web app has no calendar integration.

commercial.vendor: The Omni Group, Seattle, Washington, US. Employee-owned and private; founded in the early 1990s as a NeXT consultancy.
commercial.yearNote: 2008. OmniFocus 1.0 for Mac, released 8 January 2008; OmniFocus for the Web followed in 2019 as a companion to the Apple apps.
commercial.priceNote: OmniFocus Subscription at $99.99 a year ($8.33 a month), covering the Pro apps on every Apple device plus OmniFocus for the Web: the cheapest route to the web app without first buying a licence. Sold annually on Omni’s store; the App Store lists its $9.99 monthly and $99.99 yearly subscriptions as legacy. Owners of a perpetual licence can add web access for $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month.
commercial.freePlanNote: No free plan: a 14-day trial of the apps, and a two-week web trial that starts on first login.
commercial.plans: OmniFocus Subscription $99.99 a year from Omni’s store (Pro apps plus web); perpetual v4 licences at $74.99 Standard or $149.99 Pro, with web access an extra $49.99 a year or $4.99 a month. Since 2025 the App Store sells new buyers perpetual licences only.
commercial.hosting: Omni Sync Server (US-based vendor; region not published) holds an end-to-end encrypted copy. The Apple apps can instead sync via any WebDAV server you run, or stay local only; OmniFocus for the Web requires Omni’s sync server.
commercial.security: End-to-end sync encryption with a user-chosen passphrase; app lock on iOS; no advertising or social-media trackers. No SOC 2 or ISO 27001 claimed. No SSO, SCIM or audit log.
commercial.platforms: macOS, iOS, iPadOS, watchOS and visionOS apps, plus OmniFocus for the Web in a desktop browser (designed for computers rather than phones). No native Windows, Linux or Android apps.
commercial.ai: On-device only: optional Apple Intelligence date parsing (beta) and Siri AI reminder integration (beta) in OmniFocus 4.9, September 2026; neither runs in the web app. Omni’s privacy page says customer data is not shared with advertising or social-media services.

records.name: Paymo
records.blurb: Work management for small agencies and freelancers: tasks, time tracking, invoicing and, on the top plan, Gantt charts and team scheduling.
summary: Paymo began in 2007 inside a small web agency as a way to see where billable hours went, and it is still built around that loop: track time on tasks, then invoice the client. It suits freelancers and agencies of up to a few dozen people.

Projects hold task lists with list, table, calendar and Kanban views, plus a meta-Kanban board across projects. Time comes from in-app timers, desktop and mobile apps or the automatic Paymo Track, and feeds timesheets, estimates, invoices, expenses and profitability reports. Pro adds Gantt charts with dependencies, a portfolio Gantt, team scheduling with workload, timesheet approvals and leave planning. There is no AI and no workflow automation.

The free plan is for one person with one client and two projects. Solo costs $5.90 a month billed annually for one user; teams need Plus at $10.90 per user billed annually ($15.90 monthly), which also unlocks integrations and the API, or Pro at $16.90 for scheduling and Gantt.

Data is hosted on Amazon Web Services; Paymo publishes no certifications or region and offers no SAML SSO, though two-factor authentication and Google or Apple sign-in are available. The open REST API, with webhooks, covers all account data including comments and files, which makes a scripted exit realistic, while in-app exports are per report or table.
records.bandEvidence: Paymo says more than 50,000 agencies, firms, universities and freelancers in 100+ countries use it (paymoapp.com, about page, November 2026).
records.integrationNotes: Google Calendar and Drive, Outlook and Apple calendars, Slack, QuickBooks Online, Zapier, Make, Typeform and smaller tools such as PomoDone and LambdaTest; integrations and the REST API (with webhooks) start on Plus.
records.calendarSync: Tasks with start and due dates sync to Google Calendar as all-day events, and date or description edits made in Google flow back; new Google events do not create tasks. Google, Outlook and Apple calendar events can also be shown one way in Paymo’s My Day to log time.
records.dataOut: Reports and table views export to files, Gantt charts to PDF or PNG, invoices individually, in bulk or to QuickBooks Online and Xero. A RESTful JSON/XML API covers projects, tasks, comments, files, time entries, invoices and webhooks; Paymo points to the API for portability and backups.
records.caveat: A time-limited autumn 2026 offer for accounts created after 25 September 2026 bills monthly plans at the annual rate for the first three months; from month four Plus costs $15.90 per user.

value.review: A free single-user plan with invoicing and $10.90 a seat for teams, though Gantt and scheduling cost $16.90.

use.review: Timers, task lists and invoices are quick to pick up; scheduling and workload on Pro take more setting up.

enterprise.review: No SAML SSO, certifications or audit log; administration is user roles, guest access, optional 2FA and Google or Apple sign-in.

flex.review: List, table, calendar, Kanban and meta-Kanban views, with Gantt, workload and scheduling only on Pro; no automation.

control.review: An EU company hosting on AWS with a DPO and GDPR commitments, but no certifications and no stated region.

portability.review: The REST API reaches all account data, including comments and files, but there is no one-click account export.

gantt.note: Gantt chart, dependencies and portfolio Gantt only on Pro, the top plan.

commercial.vendor: Paymo LLC. Privately held; office in Oradea, Romania (EU).
commercial.yearNote: 2007. Year Paymo’s own history gives for its start, as a time-tracking and invoicing tool built inside a small web agency.
commercial.priceNote: Solo (one user, up to 3 clients and 5 projects), per month billed annually; $9.90 billed monthly. The team plans start with Plus at $10.90 per user billed annually.
commercial.freePlanNote: Free for 1 user with unlimited time tracking, tasks and invoices, but only 1 client, 2 projects, the list view and 1 GB of storage.
commercial.plans: Free; Solo $5.90 (one user); Plus $10.90 and Pro $16.90 per user per month billed annually ($9.90, $15.90 and $23.90 billed monthly, with the first 3 monthly months at the annual rate).
commercial.hosting: Amazon Web Services, named as the data hosting sub-processor; the region is not stated. No self-managed edition.
commercial.security: No certifications published. GDPR rights handled through the API and account deletion, a Data Protection Officer, and breach notice within 72 hours. Two-factor authentication by authenticator app or SMS code, with recovery codes; sign-in with Google or Apple accounts. No SAML SSO or audit log documented.
commercial.platforms: Web; Paymo Track desktop apps for Windows, macOS and Linux; iOS and Android apps.
commercial.ai: None.

records.name: Plaky
records.blurb: Board-based work tracker with table, Kanban, Gantt and chart views, sold by the makers of Clockify. Free for unlimited users.
summary: Plaky is a board-based work tracker from CAKE.com, the company behind the Clockify time tracker. It is aimed at small and mid-sized teams wanting a cheap, monday.com-style tool, and is free for any number of users.

Each board is a table of items with typed fields, viewable as a table, Kanban board, Gantt chart or pie and bar charts, with dashboards across boards and rule-based automations. The Gantt shows bars and subitems but no documented dependencies, and there is no calendar view or calendar sync. Time tracking works only by connecting a Clockify workspace.

The free plan has no user cap but limits boards to 6 fields and keeps a 7-day activity log. Pro at $3.99 per seat (annual) adds Gantt, unlimited fields, private boards and 1,000 automation actions a month; Enterprise at $8.99 adds SSO, board permissions and an unlimited log. The $12.99 CAKE.com Bundle includes Clockify and Pumble.

CAKE.com states ISO 27001:2022 and SOC 2 Type II at company level without naming the products covered, and says most processing is in the United States, with AWS, Microsoft and Hetzner as subprocessors; no Plaky data-region choice is documented. No AI features are listed. Leaving means per-board CSV exports, which omit comments, or the public API released in January 2026.
records.bandEvidence: CAKE.com claims 10 million+ users and 400+ employees across Clockify, Pumble and Plaky (about page, read November 2026); Plaky’s own homepage cites only 18k+ ratings and gives no separate user count.
records.integrationNotes: Integrations are CAKE.com’s own: Clockify time tracking inside items and Pumble alerts and item creation; no Slack, Zapier or calendar connectors are documented. A public API on all plans covers items, subitems and comments.
records.calendarSync: None documented: no Google or Outlook sync and no iCal feed.
records.dataOut: Any board view exports to CSV, optionally with creation-log data but without comments; CSV import creates or fills boards; the public API on all plans covers items, subitems and comments. No full-account export is documented.
records.caveat: Plaky’s Gantt has no documented dependencies and its time tracking requires a separate Clockify workspace, so teams needing scheduling or native timesheets will be paying for the bundle or another tool.

value.review: Free for unlimited users, then $3.99 a seat with no minimum; Enterprise with SSO is still under $9.

use.review: Spreadsheet-like boards with status columns that a new team can fill in within minutes.

enterprise.review: SSO, board ownership and protected views on Enterprise at $8.99; CAKE.com’s ISO 27001 and SOC 2 name no products in scope; no SCIM.

flex.review: Table, Kanban, Gantt and chart views with dashboards and automations, but no calendar view and a 6-field free cap.

control.review: Company-level ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type II without a stated Plaky scope, processing in the USA and no region choice.

portability.review: Boards export to CSV without comments, CSV import exists, and an API reaches items and comments on every plan.

tt.note: Timer and manual entries inside an item, but only through a connected Clockify workspace; reports live in Clockify.

gantt.note: Gantt view on Pro and Enterprise only, with no task dependencies documented.

commercial.vendor: CAKE.com Inc., Palo Alto, California, USA (customers outside North America contract with CAKE.com AG, Zug, Switzerland). Privately held; founded in 2009 and also makes Clockify and Pumble.
commercial.yearNote: 2022. Launch of Plaky as CAKE.com’s project management product, per the CAKE.com about page.
commercial.priceNote: Pro, per seat per month billed annually; $4.99 billed monthly. No seat minimum; up to 5 free Viewers per paid seat.
commercial.freePlanNote: Unlimited users, spaces, boards and items with table, Kanban and chart views, but only 6 fields per board, 10 MB files, a 7-day activity log and no Gantt.
commercial.plans: Free; Pro $3.99 per seat per month billed annually ($4.99 monthly); Enterprise $8.99 ($10.99); CAKE.com Bundle $12.99 ($15.99), which adds Clockify and Pumble at Enterprise level to Plaky Enterprise.
commercial.hosting: Processed mainly in the United States per the CAKE.com privacy policy, which names AWS and Microsoft (USA) and Hetzner (Germany) as infrastructure subprocessors and says customers may be offered a choice of location, including the EEA, without naming products; no Plaky data-region choice is documented, and the bundle note says Clockify data regions are not included. No self-managed edition.
commercial.security: CAKE.com’s security page (plaky.com/security redirects to it) lists ISO/IEC 27001:2022, with the certificate issued to CAKE.com Inc., and an annual SOC 2 Type II report on request, but names no products in scope; bug bounty; SSO on Enterprise, no SCIM documented; activity log kept 7 days on Free, 6 months on Pro, unlimited on Enterprise.
commercial.platforms: Web, iOS and Android.
commercial.ai: None listed on the product pages or in the 2026 changelog; the privacy policy does not address AI.

records.name: Productive
records.blurb: Agency operations platform: projects and tasks tied to budgets, time tracking, resource planning, invoicing and a sales pipeline.
summary: Productive is an operations system for agencies, consultancies and other professional services firms, joining project delivery to the money side: budgets, time, resourcing, invoicing and a sales pipeline. It suits firms of tens to hundreds of people that bill clients for time.

Projects hold task lists with boards, lists, tables, a calendar of due dates, sprints and, from Professional, a Gantt layout with dependencies. Every task, time entry and booking hangs off a budget and a service, which is what makes profitability reports, forecasting and the Scenario Builder possible, and also what makes the first setup heavier than a task tool.

Essential costs $10 per user per month billed annually ($12 monthly), with a three-seat minimum, and already includes time tracking, resource planning, expenses, docs, the API and an AI assistant with a monthly usage allowance. Professional at $25 adds the Gantt layout, approvals, rate cards and saved views; revenue forecasting, multiple subsidiaries, enforced SSO and webhooks are on Ultimate.
